historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Distrito Independencia (capital Santa Teresa del Tuy) in Miranda State on 5 December 1967, detached from Distrito Paz Castillo.
historical_names.name: Distrito Independencia

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganization of Distrito Independencia into the autonomous Municipio Independencia under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989.
historical_names.name: Independencia

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish foundation of Santa Ana de Hacarí on 14 December 1570 by Captain Francisco Fernández de Contreras.

historical_names.date_source_note: Renaming of Santa Ana de Hacarí to Ocaña in 1575 upon confirmation of its municipal status in the New Kingdom of Granada.
historical_names.name: Ocaña

historical_names.date_source_note: Foundation of Villa de San Cayetano de Chone on 7 August 1735 by Fray José Antonio Cedeño Macías.
historical_names.name: San Cayetano de Chone

historical_names.date_source_note: Cantonization of Chone on 24 July 1894 by decree of the Ecuadorian Congress under the modern name Chone.
historical_names.name: Chone

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara and Quechua settlement of Puno on the shore of Lake Titicaca prior to Spanish colonial reduction.
historical_names.name: Puno

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal establishment of the colonial parish and doctrina of San Juan Bautista de Puno in 1562, subsequently consolidated as a pueblo de indios under Viceroy Toledo's reductions in the 1570s.
historical_names.name: San Juan Bautista de Puno

historical_names.date_source_note: Official Spanish elevation to villa status and renaming to San Carlos de Puno (also styled Nuestra Señora de la Concepción y San Carlos de Puno) on 4 November 1668 by Viceroy Pedro Antonio Fernández de Castro, Count of Lemos.

historical_names.name: Puno

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Departamento Rawson in San Juan Province by Provincial Law N.º 867 on 4 September 1942 (dividing San Juan into 19 departments), named in honour of Guillermo Rawson (seat at Villa Krause).
historical_names.name: Rawson

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Carib/Meregoto settlement of Cagua (Cahúa) in the Aragua Valley prior to Spanish reduction.
historical_names.name: Cagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish foundation of the pueblo de doctrina of San José de Cagua on 29 November 1620 by Governor Francisco de la Hoz Berrío.
historical_names.name: San José de Cagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence on 5 July 1811; republican adoption of the modern name Cagua.
historical_names.name: Cagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal erection of the colonial parish of Nuestra Señora de la Encarnación del Valle de la Pascua (El Valle, south of Caracas) in 1674 (officially recognised by the Archdiocese of Caracas, with surviving parish registers from 1672; later attested in Bishop Mariano Martí's 1772 pastoral visitation).
historical_names.name: El Valle de la Pascua

historical_names.date_source_note: Incorporation as Parroquia El Valle upon the creation of the Distrito Federal of Venezuela on 8 March 1864 (attested as El Valle in the 1873 and 1941 Venezuelan censuses).
historical_names.name: El Valle

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial urban foundation of the town of San Gabriel on 8 July 1783 by Bishop Baltasar Jaime Martínez Compañón y Bujanda during his pastoral visitation of the Diocese of Trujillo.
historical_names.name: San Gabriel

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the District of Tambo Grande in Piura Province by Supreme Decree of President Agustín Gamarra on 8 October 1840, adopting the local toponym Tambo Grande (Tambogrande).
historical_names.name: Tambo Grande

historical_names.date_source_note: Erection of Distrito Guzmán Blanco (capital Cúa) in Estado Bolívar (present-day Miranda State) in 1874 during Antonio Guzmán Blanco's territorial reforms.
historical_names.name: Distrito Guzmán Blanco

historical_names.date_source_note: Official renaming of Distrito Guzmán Blanco to Distrito Cúa in 1889 following the dissolution of the Gran Estado Guzmán Blanco and creation of Miranda State.
historical_names.name: Distrito Cúa

historical_names.date_source_note: Official renaming of Distrito Cúa to Distrito Rafael Urdaneta (also known as Distrito Urdaneta, capital Cúa) on 27 July 1901 in honour of General Rafael Urdaneta.
historical_names.name: Distrito Rafael Urdaneta

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganization of Distrito Rafael Urdaneta into the autonomous Municipio Urdaneta under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989.
historical_names.name: Urdaneta

historical_names.date_source_note: Foundation of Aguachica (under the patronage of San Roque) on 16 August 1748 by José Lázaro de Rivera; attested as Aguachica in the 1793 New Granada census.
historical_names.name: Aguachica

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Quechua/Huaylas settlement of Waraq ('dawn') in the Callejón de Huaylas prior to Spanish colonial reduction.
historical_names.name: Waraq

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish foundation of the reducción of San Sebastián de Huaraz on 20 January 1574 by Captain Alonso de Santoyo y Valverde.
historical_names.name: San Sebastián de Huaraz

historical_names.date_source_note: Designation of Huaraz as capital of the Department of Huaylas under José de San Martín's Reglamento Provisional of 12 February 1821 (confirmed upon Peruvian Independence on 28 July 1821).
historical_names.name: Huaraz

historical_names.date_source_note: First urban demarcation and survey of Pueblo de La Banda (La Banda) drafted by James Oxley and Clodomiro Luque in 1888 on the left bank of the Río Dulce; officially elevated to city status on 16 September 1912 by Provincial Law N.º 392 of Santiago del Estero.
historical_names.name: La Banda

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Distrito Fraternidad (capital San Carlos del Zulia) in Zulia State on 6 October 1873, detached from Distrito Perijá (following Cantón Fraternidad of 1864).
historical_names.name: Distrito Fraternidad

historical_names.date_source_note: Official renaming of Distrito Fraternidad to Distrito Colón (capital San Carlos del Zulia) in 1881 during the territorial reorganization of Estado Falcón-Zulia (attested in the January 1891 Third National Census).
historical_names.name: Distrito Colón

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganization of Distrito Colón into the autonomous Municipio Colón under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989.
historical_names.name: Colón

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the District of Yarinacocha (capital Puerto Callao) by Ley N.º 15170 on 16 October 1964.
historical_names.name: Yarinacocha

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous settlement of Pariaguán in the Tuy Valley prior to Spanish colonial reduction.
historical_names.name: Pariaguán

historical_names.name: Santa Lucía de Pariaguán

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested under the shortened official name Santa Lucía in Bishop Mariano Martí's 1784 pastoral visitation following the town's 18th-century relocation in the Tuy Valley.
historical_names.name: Santa Lucía

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as Distrito Roscio in Guárico State in the Third National Census of Venezuela of January 1891 (capital transferred from Ortiz to San Juan de los Morros in 1934).
historical_names.name: Distrito Roscio

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganization of Distrito Roscio into the autonomous Municipio Juan Germán Roscio under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989.
historical_names.name: Juan Germán Roscio

historical_names.date_source_note: Establishment of the parish of Nuestra Señora del Rosario in the Cúcuta Valley in 1761.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Rosario

historical_names.date_source_note: Grant of the royal title of Villa del Rosario de Cúcuta by King Charles IV of Spain on 18 May 1792.
historical_names.name: Villa del Rosario de Cúcuta

historical_names.date_source_note: Official municipal designation as Villa del Rosario upon the creation of the Department of Norte de Santander by Ley 25 of 14 July 1910.
historical_names.name: Villa del Rosario

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 21 April 1831 as Villa de Ovalle by decree of Vice-President Fernando Errázuriz in the Limarí Valley, named for José Tomás Ovalle.
historical_names.name: Villa de Ovalle

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to city status (ciudad) on 22 May 1867 under President José Joaquín Pérez.
historical_names.name: Ovalle

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as an indigenous parish (reducción) of Cusco under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo, congregating Inca ayllus including Sucso and Aucaylle panacas; constituted as a republican district on 2 January 1857.
historical_names.name: San Sebastián

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Lara State (capital El Tocuyo), formalised under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989, succeeding the earlier Distrito Morán (named for Independence hero José Trinidad Morán).
historical_names.name: Morán

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as an autonomous municipality of Aragua State (capital Santa Rita) by separation from Municipio Santiago Mariño on 16 December 1997.
historical_names.name: Francisco Linares Alcántara

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muisca fortified settlement (spelled Caxicá in early Spanish chronicles) of the Zipazgo of Bacatá; reached by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada on 23 March 1537 and continuously retaining its indigenous Muisca name.
historical_names.name: Cajicá

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Pasto indigenous settlement recorded by Pedro de Cieza de León (1553) and organised as a Spanish colonial doctrina (San Pedro Mártir de Ipiales) in 1585; elevated to provincial capital of Obando in 1863.
historical_names.name: Ipiales

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Táchira State (capital Táriba), formalised under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989, succeeding the 19th-century Distrito Cárdenas.
historical_names.name: Cárdenas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Quitu-Cara and Inca settlement (llajta) in the Valle de los Chillos, retaining its indigenous name through colonial parish organisation (San Pedro de Conocoto) and civil parish codification on 29 May 1861.
historical_names.name: Conocoto

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Guárico State (capital Valle de la Pascua), formalised under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989, succeeding the former Distrito Infante (named for Independence hero Colonel Leonardo Infante).
historical_names.name: Leonardo Infante

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as an autonomous municipality of Zulia State (capital La Concepción) in 1989 by separation from the former Distrito Maracaibo under Zulia's Political-Territorial Division Law implementing Venezuela's 1989 municipal reform.
historical_names.name: Jesús Enrique Lossada

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Miranda State (capital Charallave), formalised under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989, succeeding the former Distrito Cristóbal Rojas (named for Venezuelan painter Cristóbal Rojas).
historical_names.name: Cristóbal Rojas

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Distrito de Majes (capital El Pedregal) in Caylloma Province, Arequipa, by Peruvian Law No. 27236 on 21 December 1999, following settlement of the Majes-Siguas irrigation project from the 1980s.
historical_names.name: Majes

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as a district of Tacna Province (capital Alfonso Ugarte) by Peruvian Law No. 27415 on 2 February 2001, separated from Tacna District.
historical_names.name: Coronel Gregorio Albarracín Lanchipa

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous settlement area of the Atures (Aturis) people at the Atures Rapids (Raudales de Atures) on the Orinoco River.
historical_names.name: Atures

historical_names.name: San Juan Nepomuceno de los Atures

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 9 December 1924 by engineer Santiago Aguerrevere on the centenary of the Battle of Ayacucho at the river landing near Atures; became capital of Territorio Federal Amazonas in 1928.
historical_names.name: Puerto Ayacucho

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial and early colonial Ava Guaraní (Chiriguano) endonym ('watering hole of the guan birds') for the indigenous settlement site in the western Gran Chaco foothills, settled by Ava Guaraní communities from the late 15th to 16th centuries prior to republican Bolivian establishment.
historical_names.name: Yaku-Igua

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional official founding date of the republican Bolivian settlement of Yacuiba (Hispanicised form of Guaraní Yaku-Igua), later elevated to capital of Gran Chaco Province in 1876.
historical_names.name: Yacuiba

historical_names.date_source_note: First documented mention in 1626 as a resting post (dormida/posta) on the Camino Real between Buenos Aires and Córdoba.
historical_names.name: La Dormida del Pergamino

historical_names.date_source_note: Frontier fort (Fuerte de Pergamino) and permanent settlement established around 1749–1750; erected as a parish in 1779, partido in 1784, and city on 23 October 1895.
historical_names.name: Pergamino

historical_names.date_source_note: Ecclesiastical parish founded on 3 December 1781 by Bishop Mariano Martí on the Mariara estate, incorporating the indigenous Tacarigua/Carib toponym Mariara.
historical_names.name: San Diego de Alcalá de Mariara

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened official republican name following Venezuelan Independence (also used in contemporary accounts such as Humboldt's 1800 visit); capital of Municipio Diego Ibarra since 1959.
historical_names.name: Mariara

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Aragua State (capital Cagua), formalised under Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal of 15 June 1989, succeeding the earlier Distrito Sucre (named for Antonio José de Sucre).
historical_names.name: Sucre

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban locality of Departamento Valle Viejo (Gran San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca), enumerated under this official name in the 1991 Argentine National Census (15 May 1991); no documented prior rename.

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Cantón Rumiñahui (capital Sangolquí) in Pichincha Province by Supreme Decree of General Alberto Enríquez Gallo on 31 May 1938, separated from Cantón Quito and named for Inca general Rumiñahui.

historical_names.name: Punta Cardón

historical_names.date_source_note: First Spanish foundation on 8 September 1569 by Captain Juan del Thejo, incorporating the local indigenous toponym Carora.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de la Madre de Dios de Carora

historical_names.date_source_note: Permanent refoundation on 19 June 1572 by Captain Juan de Salamanca on the Morere River.
historical_names.name: San Juan Bautista del Portillo de Carora

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened official republican name following Venezuelan Independence.
historical_names.name: Carora

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara settlement (marka) of the Pacajes (Pakaxa) polity on the Altiplano, later incorporated into the Inca Empire (Qullasuyu).
historical_names.name: Wiacha

historical_names.date_source_note: Organised as a colonial pueblo de indios and parish (San Agustín de Viacha) under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's reductions in the Corregimiento de Pacajes.
historical_names.name: San Agustín de Viacha

historical_names.date_source_note: Official republican name following Bolivian Independence (site of the Battle of Ingavi on 18 November 1841; elevated to city status on 5 December 1906).
historical_names.name: Viacha

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional official founding date (2 February 1545, Feast of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria) recognised by the municipality; attested in colonial Popayán census records by 1780 and erected as a municipality on 3 February 1864.
historical_names.name: Candelaria

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 18 November 1620 as a colonial pueblo de doctrina by Pedro Gutiérrez de Lugo and Father Gabriel de Mendoza under Governor Francisco de la Hoz Berrío.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe de La Victoria

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened official republican name following Venezuelan Independence (site of the Battle of La Victoria on 12 February 1814; capital of Municipio José Félix Ribas).
historical_names.name: La Victoria

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 8 November 1756 by Montevideo governor José Joaquín de Viana as a Spanish military camp and fort
historical_names.name: San Antonio del Salto Chico

historical_names.date_source_note: Recognized as Villa del Salto on 16 May 1835; elevated to city status on 8 June 1863
historical_names.name: Salto

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Distrito Paz Castillo of Miranda State on 14 February 1891 (reorganized as Municipio Paz Castillo in 1989–1990), with municipal seat at Santa Lucía (founded 1621)
historical_names.name: Paz Castillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Oil camp established with Lago Agrio No. 1 well on 29 March 1967; Lago Agrio Canton created on 20 June 1979 with seat at Nueva Loja (founded 5 May 1971)
historical_names.name: Lago Agrio

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1959 by José Nicolino Mattar; erected as a municipality on 22 November 1996
historical_names.name: Cumaribo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Táriba settlement first contacted by Alonso Pérez de Tolosa in 1547; congregated under Spanish colonial rule around 1602
historical_names.name: Táriba

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded as a colonial town on 24 May 1776; declared independence on 10 October 1820 and cantonized on 31 October 1955

historical_names.date_source_note: Mejía Canton established by Supreme Decree on 23 July 1883 with cantonal seat at Machachi
historical_names.name: Mejía

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 10 April 1549 by Captain Diego Palomino in the territory of the Bracamoros (Pakamuros)
historical_names.name: San Leandro de Jaén

historical_names.date_source_note: Proclaimed independence on 4 June 1821; known in republican Peru as Jaén (shortened from Jaén de Bracamoros)
historical_names.name: Jaén

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 27 April 1678 by Capuchin missionaries as Villa de San Carlos de Austria
historical_names.name: San Carlos de Austria

historical_names.date_source_note: Named capital of the newly created Province of Cojedes on 3 March 1855; shortened in republican usage to San Carlos
historical_names.name: San Carlos

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipality originally established 31 December 1812 as San Carlos
historical_names.name: San Carlos

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipal chamber renamed the municipality Ezequiel Zamora in December 2009
historical_names.name: Ezequiel Zamora

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled around 1750 as a rural district within Envigado on former Anacona indigenous lands; erected as an independent municipality on 30 November 1967 (effective 1 January 1968)
historical_names.name: Sabaneta

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Inca settlement established in the Arequipa valley under Mayta Cápac; integrated as colonial parish San Miguel de Cayma after 1540 and created as a republican district on 12 November 1823
historical_names.name: Cayma

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 31 July 1848 on ancestral Warao territory along the Mánamo River; designated capital of the Delta Federal Territory in 1888
historical_names.name: Tucupita

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded 25 April 1760 by colonial decree as Nuestra Señora del Socorro de Tinaquillo
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Socorro de Tinaquillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened in republican usage following Venezuelan independence to Tinaquillo
historical_names.name: Tinaquillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Municipio Foráneo Diego Ibarra on 30 June 1959 (elevated to autonomous municipality on 13 August 1981), with seat at Mariara (parish founded 3 December 1781)
historical_names.name: Diego Ibarra

historical_names.date_source_note: Jesuit mission of San Juan Nepomuceno de Atures founded in 1748 near the Atures Rapids
historical_names.name: San Juan Nepomuceno de Atures

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as Municipio Autónomo Atures in late 1992 following the elevation of Amazonas to statehood, with seat at Puerto Ayacucho (founded 9 December 1924)

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 23 May 1794 by Governor Ambrosio O'Higgins as Villa de San Ambrosio de Linares
historical_names.name: Villa de San Ambrosio de Linares

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated capital of the newly created Linares Province on 23 April 1873, known simply as Linares
historical_names.name: Linares

historical_names.date_source_note: District created by Law No. 23926 on 13 September 1984 (approved 12 September 1984) in Chiclayo Province
historical_names.name: La Victoria

historical_names.date_source_note: Partido created by provincial law on 25 November 1993 with administrative seat at Guernica
historical_names.name: Presidente Perón

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as a municipal entity in 1908 and reorganized as Departamento Rivadavia on 19 September 1942
historical_names.name: Rivadavia

historical_names.date_source_note: Capuchin mission settlement established in 1954 at El Coca (Puerto Francisco de Orellana)
historical_names.name: El Coca

historical_names.date_source_note: Canton Francisco de Orellana officially created on 30 April 1969 with seat at Puerto Francisco de Orellana (El Coca)
historical_names.name: Francisco de Orellana

historical_names.date_source_note: District created by Law No. 28753 on 6 June 2006 in Coronel Portillo Province, incorporating the urban area of San Fernando
historical_names.name: Manantay

historical_names.date_source_note: Initial settlement founded in August 1755 by José Joaquín de Viana and consolidated at its permanent site in 1757 as San Fernando de Maldonado
historical_names.name: San Fernando de Maldonado

historical_names.date_source_note: Transitioned to official name Maldonado upon Uruguayan independence (Preliminary Peace Convention of 27 August 1828)
historical_names.name: Maldonado

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Picunche and Inca provincial agricultural center (wamani) in the Aconcagua Valley prior to Spanish conquest
historical_names.name: Quillota

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally founded as Villa de San Martín de la Concha del Valle de Quillota (decree 19 August 1717, civic foundation 11 November 1717)
historical_names.name: Villa de San Martín de la Concha

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to city status on 6 August 1822 by Bernardo O'Higgins as Ciudad de San Martín de Quillota, thereafter known simply as Quillota
historical_names.name: Quillota

historical_names.date_source_note: District officially created on 16 November 1992 on the slopes of Misti volcano in Arequipa Province
historical_names.name: Alto Selva Alegre

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Municipio Urbano de la Costa via Buenos Aires Provincial Decree-Law 9024 of 11 June 1978, detached from Partido de General Lavalle (reconstituted as Partido de La Costa by Law 9949 of 26 May 1983).
historical_names.name: La Costa

historical_names.date_source_note: Jesuit mission reduction founded on 8 December 1709 at the Huallaga-Shanusi-Paranapura confluence for migrated Yurimagua indigenous communities under Father Samuel Fritz.

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated under its civil name Yurimaguas as capital of the newly created Province of Alto Amazonas by Peruvian Decree of 7 February 1866 (ratified by Law of 11 September 1868).
historical_names.name: Yurimaguas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Caquetío and Gayón indigenous toponym of the Yaritagua valley prior to Spanish colonial consolidation.
historical_names.name: Yaritagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial town and ecclesiastical parish of Santa Lucía de Yaritagua established under Spanish administration (traditional founding date 13 December 1699).
historical_names.name: Santa Lucía de Yaritagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated under its civil name Yaritagua as head of Cantón Yaritagua upon the creation of the Province of Yaracuy by Venezuelan Legislative Decree of 19 March 1855; modern capital of Municipio Peña.
historical_names.name: Yaritagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial Spanish town founded on 14 July 1650 by Captain Buenaventura de la Peña on the ejidos (common lands) of Mérida.
historical_names.name: San Buenaventura de Ejido

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to the rank of Villa de Ejido by the Patriotic Junta of Mérida on 18 September 1811.
historical_names.name: Ejido

historical_names.date_source_note: Territorial jurisdiction renamed Campo Elías (Departamento, later Distrito and Municipio Campo Elías, seat at Ejido) under the Mérida State Territorial Division Law of 28 December 1868, honouring Vicente Campo Elías.
historical_names.name: Campo Elías

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial rural settlement and chapel recorded as Laguna de la Reducción in the 1744 Buenos Aires rural census within the Pago de la Magdalena.
historical_names.name: Laguna de la Reducción

historical_names.name: San Vicente

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Pasto indigenous endonym (Hulcán) in the Andean highlands of Carchi prior to Spanish conquest.

historical_names.date_source_note: Cantonisation of Tulcán on 11 April 1851 by the National Convention of Ecuador; capital of Carchi Province since 19 November 1880.

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Mapudungun endonym (Wallpen) for the Mapuche-Lafkenche peninsula at the mouth of the Biobío River.
historical_names.name: Wallpen

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish-orthography locality and estate of Hualpén bequeathed to public stewardship upon the death of Pedro del Río Zañartu on 26 April 1918; constituted as the independent Commune of Hualpén by Chilean Law 19.936 on 13 March 2004.
historical_names.name: Hualpén

historical_names.date_source_note: Already standard as Nirgua in late colonial sources (including the 1769 colonial census) and formally designated Cantón Nirgua under Gran Colombia's Law of Territorial Division of 25 June 1824.

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 19 February 1715 by Domingo de Castro y Bazán as Villa Santa Rita de la Piedra.

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern settlement founded around 1878 (exact day/month unrecorded) on Carib/Chaima territory near the former 18th-century mission site of Nueva Palencia; became capital of Distrito (now Municipio) Bolívar on 30 January 1940.
historical_names.name: Caripito

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara altiplano settlement known as Llaxaa / Laxa prior to Inca and Spanish arrival (approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Llaxaa

historical_names.date_source_note: Site where Captain Alonso de Mendoza signed the founding act of Nuestra Señora de La Paz on 20 October 1548 before relocating the city to Chuquiago Marka days later; the altiplano town persisted under the Hispanicised name Laja.
historical_names.name: Laja

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muchik (Mochica/Chimú-era) settlement at Chuspo/Alicán within the Cinto chiefdom prior to Spanish colonial reduction (approximate pre-contact date; Muchik endonym later recorded as Omænssæfæc).
historical_names.name: Chuspo

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción de indios at Callanca (Cinto chiefdom), severely damaged by the 1578 El Niño floods and abandoned after the 1612 epidemic.
historical_names.name: Callanca

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocation and establishment of Monsefú (Hispanicised from Muchik Omænssæfæc) by survivors of the 1612 Callanca epidemic (exact day/month unrecorded); elevated to city on 26 October 1888.
historical_names.name: Monsefú

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 12 October 1953 by Lieutenant Jaime Fernández Salazar and displaced settlers from the ruined town of Moreno (earlier La Fragua), named for the 1953 Llanos peace accords; erected as a municipality on 12 October 1974.
historical_names.name: Paz de Ariporo

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern oil-camp settlement formally established in 1938 by Royal Dutch Shell / Venezuelan Oil Concessions on the eastern shore of Lake Maracaibo adjacent to ancestral indigenous palafito waters (exact day/month unrecorded); constituted as capital of the autonomous Municipality of Valmore Rodríguez in 1989 (law of 21 July 1989, implemented 11 December 1989 / 1989.12.11).
historical_names.name: Bachaquero

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 20 January 1576 by Captain Francisco Redondo Ponce de León on Gorrones indigenous territory as Villa de Cáceres.
historical_names.name: Villa de Cáceres

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated in 1602 (exact day/month unrecorded) to the Estancia de Roldanillo due to indigenous resistance, becoming San Sebastián de Roldanillo and subsequently Roldanillo.
historical_names.name: Roldanillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as Municipio Castro on 29 July 1904 under President Cipriano Castro, with Las Tejerías as its seat.
historical_names.name: Castro

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Municipio Tejerías (later Municipio Foráneo Las Tejerías) in November 1909 following the fall of Cipriano Castro (exact day unrecorded).
historical_names.name: Tejerías

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to autonomous Municipio Autónomo Santos Michelena by the Legislative Assembly of Aragua State on 23 October 1986, retaining Las Tejerías as its capital.
historical_names.name: Santos Michelena

historical_names.date_source_note: Franciscan river mission and settlement of Puerto Ocopa consolidated in 1919 on ancestral Asháninka territory (exact day/month unrecorded), serving as initial administrative seat when Río Tambo District was created.
historical_names.name: Puerto Ocopa

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Río Tambo formally created by Law No. 9801 on 29 January 1943 (initially in Jauja Province, later Satipo Province), with Puerto Ocopa as provisional seat and subsequently Puerto Prado.
historical_names.name: Río Tambo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muisca settlement (Paypa, within the Cacicazgo de Tundama) prior to Spanish conquest (earliest_year 1100 anchor; approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Paypa

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal Spanish colonial urban and doctrinal foundation decreed by visitador Luis Enríquez on 19 February 1602 (following initial 1539 Spanish encomienda contact).
historical_names.name: Paipa

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional founding date of Güiria (8 December 1767, Feast of the Immaculate Conception), colonial settlement on the Gulf of Paria and urban seat of the future Valdez municipality
historical_names.name: Güiria

historical_names.date_source_note: Enactment of Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (15 June 1989), establishing the autonomous Municipio Valdez (formerly Distrito Valdez, named after General Manuel Valdez) with Güiria as its seat
historical_names.name: Valdez

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional founding date (8 September 1709, Feast of Nuestra Señora de Regla) of the settlement of Nuestra Señora de Regla in the Mocotíes Valley
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de Regla

historical_names.date_source_note: Decree of 19 April 1850 elevating Nuestra Señora de Regla to Villa de Tovar in honour of Venezuelan statesman Martín Tovar Ponte
historical_names.name: Tovar

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1783 by Rafael Pérez del Puerto under orders of Viceroy Juan José de Vértiz y Salcedo; no single founding-act day survives in colonial records
historical_names.name: Villa de la Concepción de las Minas

historical_names.date_source_note: Uruguayan Law No. 1,980 of 16 May 1888 formally elevating Villa de la Concepción de las Minas to the category of city as Minas
historical_names.name: Minas

historical_names.date_source_note: Construction of Fort San José de Alcudia in 1793 under Governor Ambrosio O'Higgins on the Río Bueno (Mapudungun Wenuleufu) following the destruction of the 1778 mission; exact dedication day varies in colonial sources
historical_names.name: San José de Alcudia

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the autonomous Comuna de Río Bueno by Supreme Decree of 22 December 1891 under Chile's Ley de Comuna Autónoma
historical_names.name: Río Bueno

historical_names.date_source_note: Capuchin mission of Santo Tomás de Tucupido founded c. 1760 (attested in Bishop Mariano Martí's pastoral visitation records), seat of the future municipality; exact founding day and month are unattested
historical_names.name: Santo Tomás de Tucupido

historical_names.date_source_note: Enactment of Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (15 June 1989), establishing the autonomous Municipio José Félix Ribas in Guárico State (seat: Tucupido)
historical_names.name: José Félix Ribas

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal erection of the ecclesiastical parish of San Francisco de Paula de Yare on 8 February 1714 by the ecclesiastical cabildo of Caracas
historical_names.name: San Francisco de Paula de Yare

historical_names.date_source_note: First National Census of Venezuela (7–9 November 1873), officially recording the shortened republican parish name San Francisco de Yare (later seat of Municipio Simón Bolívar)
historical_names.name: San Francisco de Yare

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción of Yauri (Quechua Yawri, on pre-Hispanic K'ana territory) organized under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement of Cusco (c. 1571–1572); exact day and month are unattested
historical_names.name: Yauri

historical_names.date_source_note: Peruvian Law No. 2542 of 17 November 1917 creating Espinar Province and District (named for Colonel Ladislao Espinar) with Yauri as its capital
historical_names.name: Espinar

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Juanjuí on 24 September 1827 (Feast of Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes) along the Huallaga River
historical_names.name: Juanjuí

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement founded c. 1914 in the San Jorge basin (elevated to a municipality of Córdoba in 1956); exact day and month of initial settlement are unattested
historical_names.name: Pueblo Nuevo

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the pueblo de doctrina of San Mateo on 30 November 1620 by Governor Francisco de la Hoz Berrío in the Aragua Valley
historical_names.name: San Mateo

historical_names.date_source_note: Enactment of Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (15 June 1989), establishing the autonomous Municipio Bolívar in Aragua State with San Mateo as its seat
historical_names.name: Bolívar

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement originated c. 1920 around the Puerto Wilches railway station (erected as a municipality of Santander by Ordinance No. 02 of 24 November 1973); exact day and month of initial settlement are unattested
historical_names.name: Sabana de Torres

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal erection of the parish of Río Chico (Nuestra Señora de las Mercedes) on 24 September 1791 by Bishop Mariano Martí
historical_names.name: Río Chico

historical_names.date_source_note: Enactment of Venezuela's Ley Orgánica de Régimen Municipal (15 June 1989), establishing the autonomous Municipio Páez in Miranda State (formerly Distrito Páez, seat: Río Chico)
historical_names.name: Páez

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Chimichagua (as Nuestra Señora de la Concepción de Chimichagua) on 8 December 1748 by José Fernando de Mier y Guerra on Chimila indigenous territory
historical_names.name: Chimichagua

historical_names.date_source_note: Early river settlement at the Ovejas–Cauca confluence within Buenos Aires, Cauca (traditional founding date 29 July 1823; consolidated c. 1880), known locally as Ovejas prior to the arrival of the Ferrocarril del Pacífico
historical_names.name: Ovejas

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Suárez during President Marco Fidel Suárez's 1918–1921 administration upon arrival of the Ferrocarril del Pacífico station (erected as a separate municipality from Buenos Aires on 1 December 1989); exact day and month of renaming are unattested
historical_names.name: Suárez

historical_names.date_source_note: Mid-19th-century origin of the fishing and goat-dairy settlement of Lechería near El Morro de Barcelona, urban seat of the future municipality; exact founding year, month, and day are unattested
historical_names.name: Lechería

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Municipio Turístico El Morro Licenciado Diego Bautista Urbaneja (short name: Diego Bautista Urbaneja, seat: Lechería) by the Legislative Assembly of Anzoátegui State on 22 January 1992
historical_names.name: Diego Bautista Urbaneja

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonization settlement of La Hormiga established c. 1956 in the Guamuez River valley; exact day and month of initial settlement are unattested
historical_names.name: La Hormiga

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the Municipality of Valle del Guamuez (seat: La Hormiga) on 27 November 1985 by Decree No. 2830
historical_names.name: Valle del Guamuez

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the parish of Santa Ana del Guamo on 26 June 1772 by Father Juan Antonio de Buenaventura y Castillo
historical_names.name: Santa Ana del Guamo

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the Sovereign State of Tolima (12 April 1861), in which the town (and interim state capital) was officially designated under the shortened republican name Guamo
historical_names.name: Guamo

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Fuerte y Población de Nuestra Señora del Carmen on 22 April 1779 by Francisco de Viedma y Narváez on the Río Negro
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Carmen

historical_names.date_source_note: Argentine Law No. 954 of 11 October 1878 creating the Gobernación de la Patagonia on the south bank, formally demarcating Partido de Patagones (seat: Carmen de Patagones) on the north bank in Buenos Aires Province
historical_names.name: Patagones

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern town originated with the founding of Colonia Bolívar in the Araira Valley by decree of President Antonio Guzmán Blanco on 21 September 1874, retaining the indigenous-derived valley name Araira
historical_names.name: Araira

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the river port of Atalaya on 29 May 1928 by Francisco Vargas Hernández at the confluence of the Tambo and Urubamba rivers
historical_names.name: Atalaya

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the District of Raymondi (capital: Atalaya) by Peruvian Law No. 9815 of 2 July 1943
historical_names.name: Raymondi

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the Capuchin mission of Nuestra Señora de la Paz de Guanarito on 24 January 1768 by Fray Andrés de Grazalema
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de la Paz de Guanarito

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Portuguesa Province (promulgated 15 April 1851), formally establishing the republican Canton of Guanarito under the shortened name Guanarito
historical_names.name: Guanarito

historical_names.date_source_note: Original colonial parish of Guayabal de la Mesa established in 1649 prior to its 1777 relocation to the Mesa de Juan Díaz plateau; exact day and month are unattested
historical_names.name: Guayabal

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding and relocation of the parish to the Mesa de Juan Díaz plateau (as Santa Bárbara de La Mesa de Juan Díaz) on 12 March 1777 under Viceroy Manuel Antonio Flórez
historical_names.name: Mesa de Juan Díaz

historical_names.date_source_note: Gran Colombia's Ley de División Territorial (25 June 1824), formally designating the shortened republican name La Mesa as a canton seat of Bogotá Province
historical_names.name: La Mesa

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial settlement of San Nicolás de Obispos established in 1713 near Barinas; exact founding day and month are unattested
historical_names.name: San Nicolás de Obispos

historical_names.date_source_note: Gran Colombia's Ley de División Territorial (25 June 1824), formally establishing Cantón Obispos in Barinas Province under the shortened name Obispos
historical_names.name: Obispos

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Villa Gesell on 14 December 1931 by Carlos Idaho Gesell on the Atlantic coast of Buenos Aires Province (separated as an independent partido in 1978)
historical_names.name: Villa Gesell

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of San Martín de los Andes on 4 February 1898 by General Rudecindo Roca and Colonel Celestino Pérez on the shore of Lake Lácar
historical_names.name: San Martín de los Andes

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 20 January 1920 by Capuchin Father Estanislao de Las Corts and Special Commissioner Braulio Eraso Chávez as Caucayá on the Putumayo River (named after the nearby Caucayá stream).
historical_names.name: Caucayá

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally constituted as the municipality of Puerto Leguízamo by Decree No. 13 of 22 January 1958, following adoption of the name after the 1949 fire in honour of Colombia–Peru War soldier Cándido Leguízamo Bonilla.
historical_names.name: Puerto Leguízamo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Chancay and Inca settlement of Wawra (Hispanicised as Huaura/Huara) in the Huaura River valley, attested prior to Spanish foundation.
historical_names.name: Wawra

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded as Villa de Carrión de Velasco on 25 July 1597 by order of Viceroy Luis de Velasco y Castilla (verified by the original Acta de Fundación preserved in the Archivo del Obispado de Huacho).
historical_names.name: Villa de Carrión de Velasco

historical_names.date_source_note: Established under the republican name Huaura by General José de San Martín's Reglamento Provisional of 12 February 1821 issued at Huaura.
historical_names.name: Huaura

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding date (25 February 1906), marking the arrival of the telegraph to the Patagonian settlement whose name derives from the Tehuelche toponym Esquel.
historical_names.name: Esquel

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muisca settlement (from Muysccubun pa-cho, 'good father'); organised as a colonial pueblo de indios from 1604 (traditional Hispanic foundation 6 January 1642) and erected as a municipality in 1807.
historical_names.name: Pacho

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 17 October 1774 at Sitio Viejo (present-day Damasco), relocated to Alto de Cienegueta on 18 October 1816, and erected as a municipality in 1822.
historical_names.name: Santa Bárbara

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional founding date (22 September 1735), corresponding to the colonial land grant (merced) of Cruz del Eje in northwestern Córdoba.
historical_names.name: Cruz del Eje

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1853 as La Fría in Táchira State; later developed as the terminus of the Gran Ferrocarril del Táchira (1895) and serves as capital of Municipio García de Hevia.
historical_names.name: La Fría

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial settlement and parish established by 1745 in the Mocaná region of Cartagena province under the patronage of Santo Tomás de Villanueva.
historical_names.name: Santo Tomás de Villanueva

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as a republican municipality under the shortened official name Santo Tomás within the Sovereign State of Bolívar in 1857.
historical_names.name: Santo Tomás

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 20 November 1889 by Guillermo Allende on lands of the Allende family estate (Estancia San Alfonso) in the Sierras Chicas of Córdoba.
historical_names.name: Villa Allende

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional colonial foundation date (27 June 1676) of the coastal settlement and later Municipio Punta de Piedras on Margarita Island, Nueva Esparta.
historical_names.name: Punta de Piedras

historical_names.date_source_note: Decree of 22 December 1915 by Nueva Esparta State President General Juan Alberto Ramírez renaming Municipio Punta de Piedras to Municipio Tubores in honour of Venezuelan War of Independence officer Coronel José Celedonio Tubores (1771–1817); later elevated to Distrito Tubores on 27 June 1976.
historical_names.name: Tubores

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Chui and Quechua settlement in the Cochabamba valleys; administered as the colonial parish of San Pedro de Aiquile and retained as Aiquile in the Republic of Bolivia (1825; capital of Campero Province from 1899).
historical_names.name: Aiquile

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally created as the municipality of Albania by Departmental Ordinance No. 001 of 19 March 2000, segregated from Maicao in La Guajira (previously a 20th-century corregimiento of Maicao in Wayuu territory).
historical_names.name: Albania

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Guane settlement and chiefdom of Chanchón prior to Spanish conquest (1540).
historical_names.name: Chanchón

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 16 June 1683 as Nuestra Señora del Socorro by José de Archila and José Díaz Sarmiento (granted villa status in 1771).
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Socorro

historical_names.date_source_note: Proclaimed independence on 10 July 1810 and administered in the republican era under the shortened official name Socorro.
historical_names.name: Socorro

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 8 December 1767 by Capuchin missionaries on the Paria Peninsula under the patronage of the Immaculate Conception, retaining the indigenous Paria/Chaima toponym Güiria.
historical_names.name: Güiria

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1917 as a settlement in the upper Sinú valley; segregated from Tierralta and established as a municipality of Córdoba Department in 1959 (effective 1960).
historical_names.name: Valencia

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 1 June 1783 by Lieutenant Eusebio Vidal with Asturian and Leonese colonists as Villa de San José in the Banda Oriental.
historical_names.name: Villa de San José

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to city status and officially designated San José de Mayo by Law No. 495 of 12 July 1856.
historical_names.name: San José de Mayo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Quechua settlement in the Valle Alto of Cochabamba; recorded as the parish of Punata (San Juan Bautista de Punata) in the late 18th century (including Francisco de Viedma's 1793 report), elevated to Villa de Punata on 18 May 1838 and to city status as Punata on 19 January 1900.
historical_names.name: Punata

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 30 April 1830 by Kukama-Kukamiria leader Manuel Pacaya Irarica near the Marañón–Ucayali confluence in Loreto.
historical_names.name: Nauta

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1591 by Captain Gonzalo de Piña Ludueña as Nuestra Señora de Altagracia de Pedraza in the Barinas foothills.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de Altagracia de Pedraza

historical_names.date_source_note: Rebuilt in 1617 on the Canaguá River following indigenous Jirajara attacks and administered thereafter as Pedraza through the colonial and 19th-century republican eras.
historical_names.name: Pedraza

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Ciudad Bolivia by the mid-20th century in Barinas State territorial legislation, while the surrounding municipality retained the historical name Municipio Pedraza.
historical_names.name: Ciudad Bolivia

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Aymara and Quechua settlement (Payaqullu) in the highlands of Cinti (Chuquisaca).
historical_names.name: Payacollo

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial parish (doctrina) established in the Partido de Pilaya y Paspaya (Cinti), combining the patron saint San Lucas with the indigenous toponym Payacollo.
historical_names.name: San Lucas de Payacollo

historical_names.date_source_note: Administered under the shortened official name San Lucas in the Republic of Bolivia (independence 6 August 1825), later municipal seat in Nor Cinti Province.
historical_names.name: San Lucas

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally founded on 30 November 1821 by Father Nicolás Ramírez in southern Tolima (ancestral Pijao territory, in the vicinity of the destroyed 1572 colonial outpost of Santiago de la Frontera).
historical_names.name: Ortega

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested coastal settlement of Esmeraldas, site of the 5 August 1820 Esmeraldas independence proclamation; elevated to cantonal seat (Cantón Rioverde) on 22 July 1996.
historical_names.name: Rioverde

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Palta settlement of Cangochamba in the Catamayo valley prior to Spanish arrival.
historical_names.name: Cangochamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Temporary Spanish foundation of La Zarza established in August 1546 by Captain Alonso de Mercadillo in the Cangochamba/Catamayo valley prior to relocating Loja to the Cuxibamba valley in 1548.
historical_names.name: La Zarza

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal erection of the civil parish of La Toma on 25 May 1931, named after the colonial and republican Hacienda La Toma that developed in the valley.
historical_names.name: La Toma

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to cantonal seat as Catamayo on 22 May 1981, adopting the indigenous Palta valley toponym.
historical_names.name: Catamayo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Aymara and Quechua settlement (Tapaqari) in western Cochabamba; reorganised as a Viceroy Toledo reducción de indios in the 1570s (patronal title San Agustín de Tapacarí), documented as Tapacarí in Francisco de Viedma's 1793 census, and retained as Tapacarí in the Republic of Bolivia.
historical_names.name: Tapacarí

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Mapuche settlement and territory (Mapudungun pangi-pülli, 'hill/land of pumas') on Lake Panguipulli; consolidated around the 1903 Capuchin mission and formally constituted as the comuna of Panguipulli by Law No. 8,707 of 24 December 1946.
historical_names.name: Panguipulli

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara settlement of the Quillacas-Azanaques señorío on the sandy plateau east of Lake Poopó.
historical_names.name: Ch'allapata

historical_names.date_source_note: Early colonial-indigenous settlement recorded c. 1560 at the foot of Cerro Quiwiri along the Cagually River prior to the 1573 Toledo census.
historical_names.name: Chimpa Cagually

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial Spanish parish foundation and church consecration under San Juan Bautista in June 1700.
historical_names.name: San Juan Bautista de Challapata

historical_names.date_source_note: Official republican foundation of the modern town promulgated by law on 23 August 1893 alongside the Oruro-Uyuni railway.
historical_names.name: Challapata

historical_names.date_source_note: First colonial settlement founded c. 1608–1612 by Pedro Sáenz de la Guía in Mulale and Laculata indigenous territory; later abandoned due to Andaquí raids and officially refounded on 20 November 1790.
historical_names.name: San Agustín

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 8 March 1834 by Juan Nepomuceno Mosquera as Bocas de San Pablo, also known as San Pablo.
historical_names.name: Bocas de San Pablo

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Istmina by Law 5 of 1903 upon becoming capital of the San Juan province.
historical_names.name: Istmina

historical_names.date_source_note: Rubber-era settlement established c. 1914 at the confluence of the Huallaga and Tocache rivers.
historical_names.name: San Juan de Tocache

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated to higher ground after severe floods in 1936–1937 as Tocache Nuevo.
historical_names.name: Tocache Nuevo

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to district capital as Tocache by Law No. 9097 on 7 May 1940.
historical_names.name: Tocache

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional settlement of Muey formally elevated to a rural parish of Salinas canton by Decree No. 115 on 22 December 1937.
historical_names.name: Muey

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed in honour of former President José Luis Tamayo by Ministerial Accord No. 255 on 14 May 1948.
historical_names.name: José Luis Tamayo

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality created by the Legislative Assembly of Lara State on 9 October 1990, with Sarare as its capital.
historical_names.name: Simón Planas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Quechua toponym of the Lluchos and Huamachuco territory prior to Spanish conquest.
historical_names.name: Kashapampa

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial Spanish reduction founded on 10 September 1572 under Viceroy Toledo's ordinances.
historical_names.name: San Nicolás de Tolentino de Caxabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to republican villa as Cajabamba on 12 November 1827 and subsequently to city on 9 November 1839.
historical_names.name: Cajabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Indigenous Asháninka river-valley toponym formalised as district capital by Law No. 15481 on 26 March 1965.
historical_names.name: Mazamari

historical_names.date_source_note: Catalan Capuchin mission founded on 26 January 1788 by Fray Mariano de Perafita in Guayano and Kamaracoto territory.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de Belén de Tumeremo

historical_names.date_source_note: Secularised civil settlement under the Republic of Venezuela following the 1817 collapse of the Caroní Capuchin missions.
historical_names.name: Tumeremo

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban town formally founded on 31 July 1863 as seat of the partido of Saladillo created on 25 December 1839.
historical_names.name: Saladillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 26 May 1859 on lands donated by Guillermo Sierra from the Hacienda de Metán, pairing the parish patron San José with the Lule-derived toponym Metán.
historical_names.name: San José de Metán

historical_names.date_source_note: Frontier fort and settlement established on 8 November 1836 by Lieutenant Colonel Juan Isidro Quesada.
historical_names.name: Cantón de las Mulitas

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed partido De la Encarnación in 1847 under Governor Juan Manuel de Rosas.
historical_names.name: De la Encarnación

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed 25 de Mayo by decree of Governor Pastor Obligado in 1853.
