historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and parish organised in Chayanta (Charcas) under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement (c. 1572–1575; exact day not independently confirmed), attested in colonial ecclesiastical and mining records of Charcas as San Salvador de Ocurí (Asiento de Minas de San Salvador de Ocurí).
historical_names.name: San Salvador de Ocurí

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally listed under the shortened republican civil name Cantón Ocurí within Chayanta Province by the Bolivian Law of 3 September 1880 reorganising Chayanta and Charcas (having already figured as a canton in 19th-century republican Chayanta), and later constituted as an autonomous municipality (Fourth Municipal Section of Chayanta Province) by Law 257 of 16 November 1963.
historical_names.name: Ocurí

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous settlement (Calamarí/Mokaná territory in the hinterland of Cartagena) documented prior to Spanish colonisation and preceding the colonial town of Santa Rosa.
historical_names.name: Alipaya

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial parish established c. 1735 on the site of indigenous Alipaya in the Province of Cartagena (attested in the 1778–1779 Cartagena provincial census); known concurrently as Santa Rosa and Santa Rosa de Lima without a separate modern rename.
historical_names.name: Santa Rosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement established c. 1872–1876 (exact day not independently confirmed) by Afro-Colombian settlers acquiring plots on lands of the historical hacienda of Guachené within the jurisdiction of Caloto, Cauca (continuing the indigenous toponym associated with Cacique Guachené); long administered as a corregimiento of Caloto before gaining municipal autonomy on 19 December 2006 by Decreto Ordenanza 0653 of the Governor of Cauca.
historical_names.name: Guachené

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Zenú indigenous settlement (site of the Momil archaeological complex and Cacique Momil) on the Ciénaga Grande del Bajo Sinú, preceding Spanish colonisation.
historical_names.name: Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Refounded and reorganised as a Spanish colonial settlement on 17 November 1776 by Antonio de la Torre y Miranda under the name San Antonio de Momil in the Province of Cartagena.
historical_names.name: San Antonio de Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally constituted as Municipio de Momil in Córdoba Department by Departmental Ordenanza 021 of 21 August 1963 (segregated from Purísima), establishing the shortened modern official municipal name (used earlier in republican administration alongside San Antonio de Momil).
historical_names.name: Momil

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and parish founded in the Corregimiento of Larecaja (Kallawaya valley region, La Paz) under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement (c. 1572–1575; exact day not independently confirmed), documented in colonial ecclesiastical and visita records as San Pedro de Mocomoco.
historical_names.name: San Pedro de Mocomoco

historical_names.date_source_note: Incorporated as Cantón Mocomoco within the newly created Province of Muñecas by Bolivian Law of 18 October 1826 (signed by President Antonio José de Sucre, dividing Larecaja), establishing the shortened republican civil name (later transferred to Eliodoro Camacho Province by Law of 5 November 1908).
historical_names.name: Mocomoco

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous Municipality of Libertador (Táchira State, capital Abejales) created in 1972 by the Legislative Assembly of Táchira, segregated from Uribante (exact month and day not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: Libertador

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 4 August 1791 as a Franciscan mission settlement along the Uchiza River in the Alto Huallaga by Fray Manuel Sobreviela (Guardian of the Colegio de Ocopa) with 16 Cholón families, contemporaneously documented in Mercurio Peruano (1791); later constituted as Distrito de Uchiza by Peruvian Law 1595 on 21 October 1912.
historical_names.name: Uchiza

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as Departamento de Perico del Carmen in 1851 around the 18th-century chapel settlement of Nuestra Señora del Carmen in the Valle de Perico, Jujuy (recorded as Perico del Carmen in the 1869 and 1895 Argentine national censuses).
historical_names.name: Perico del Carmen

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially designated El Carmen by the early 20th century, as recorded in the Third Argentine National Census of 1 June 1914 (shortened from Perico del Carmen to distinguish it from Estación Perico; exact provincial decree date between 1895 and 1914 not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: El Carmen

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 24 March 1950 by José Francisco Rojas Guerra along the Troncal de Occidente highway in the San Jorge subregion (then part of Ayapel); later elevated to an independent municipality of Córdoba Department by Departmental Ordinance 010 of 13 November 1969.
historical_names.name: Buenavista

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled and founded as Balboa in 1912 in the Patía region of Cauca (named after Vasco Núñez de Balboa; exact month and day not independently confirmed), later elevated to an independent municipality in 1967.
historical_names.name: Balboa

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 15 August 1563 in the Upano Valley (Shuar and Macas indigenous territory) as Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Macas; survivors of the 1599 destruction of nearby Sevilla de Oro later consolidated here.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Macas

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated Macas (Cantón Macas) in the 25 June 1824 Ley de División Territorial of Gran Colombia, establishing the modern republican name (now capital of Morona Santiago Province and Cantón Morona).
historical_names.name: Macas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Panzaleo/Sigchos chiefdom in the western highlands of Cotopaxi, preceding Spanish colonisation.
historical_names.name: Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as the Spanish colonial parish (doctrina) of San Miguel de Sigchos within the Corregimiento of Latacunga in the late 16th century (exact founding day not independently confirmed).
historical_names.name: San Miguel de Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally constituted as the civil parish of Sigchos under Ecuador's Ley de División Territorial of 29 May 1861 (elevated to Cantón Sigchos on 21 July 1992).
historical_names.name: Sigchos

historical_names.date_source_note: Partido de Saavedra created on 10 September 1891 by Buenos Aires Provincial Law 2421 (named after Cornelio Saavedra; its eponymous railway town originated in 1884–1888, and Pigüé later became the partido seat in 1934).
historical_names.name: Saavedra

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 19 November 1732 by resolution of the Cabildo of Corrientes as San José de las Siete Lagunas Saladas (in the Pago de las Saladas, former Guaraní territory).
historical_names.name: San José de las Siete Lagunas Saladas

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally designated Saladas in the 11 December 1821 Provisional Constitution (Reglamento Provisorio) of the Province of Corrientes, adopting the shortened modern name.
historical_names.name: Saladas

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as Distrito Mariño (capital Irapa, on the Paria Peninsula; named after General Santiago Mariño) within restored Sucre State under Venezuela's Constitution of 5 August 1909, becoming Municipio Mariño under the 1989 municipal reform.
historical_names.name: Mariño

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 6 November 1659 as San Pedro in the Norte antioqueño (former Nutabe indigenous territory); erected as a parish in 1757 and as a municipality of Antioquia in 1813. Although the venerated image of the Señor de los Milagros arrived around 1774 and parish priest Fermín de Hoyos (with Padre Marianito) began building the present Basilica in 1874, the municipality remained officially named San Pedro until 2001.
historical_names.name: San Pedro

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed San Pedro de los Milagros on 12 December 2001 by Asamblea Departamental de Antioquia Ordenanza N.° 29 de 2001 ('Por medio de la cual se le adiciona el nombre a un municipio del Departamento de Antioquia'), formalising the long-standing devotional title.
historical_names.name: San Pedro de los Milagros

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 2 July 1857 by General Justo José de Urquiza as an agricultural colony of Swiss, Savoyard, and Piedmontese immigrants in Entre Ríos.
historical_names.name: Colonia San José

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally elevated to villa status as Villa San José in 1894 during the governorship of Entre Ríos Governor Sabá Z. Hernández (1891–1895; exact decree day in 1894 not independently confirmed), achieving local separation from Colón; its first Junta de Fomento took office on 8 January 1904 under Governor Enrique Carbó Ortiz, and it became a 2nd-category municipality on 1 July 1935.
historical_names.name: Villa San José

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to a 1st-category municipality (Ciudad de San José) on 4 October 1957 under Entre Ríos provincial administration, establishing the modern official municipal name San José.
historical_names.name: San José

historical_names.date_source_note: Provincial law of Buenos Aires creating Partido de Juárez, officially celebrated as the town's founding date
historical_names.name: Benito Juárez

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Yampara and Inca indigenous settlement (Quechua: Tarapuku) prior to Spanish reducción
historical_names.name: Tarapuku

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish Toledan reducción founded on the feast of Saint Peter (29 June 1578)
historical_names.name: San Pedro de Tarabuco

historical_names.date_source_note: Bolivian independence and republican canton/town name
historical_names.name: Tarabuco

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 1 May 1936 in Cesar (elevated to municipality in 1984)
historical_names.name: Astrea

historical_names.date_source_note: Established in 1722 upon relocation of settlers from Anserma to northern Valle del Cauca (municipality since 1925)
historical_names.name: Ansermanuevo

historical_names.date_source_note: Ley N° 23832 creating Condorcanqui Province and Río Santiago District (capital Puerto Galilea)
historical_names.name: Río Santiago

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of La Quiaca by Jujuy Provincial Law N° 134 alongside railway arrival
historical_names.name: La Quiaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Las Lomitas (Formosa) with the arrival of the Ramal C25 railway
historical_names.name: Las Lomitas

historical_names.date_source_note: Initial settlement established on 19 December 1830 in the Comiá valley
historical_names.name: La Comiá

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Concordia upon creation as a parish and district in 1848
historical_names.name: Concordia

historical_names.date_source_note: Distrito (later Municipio) Rafael Rangel established in Trujillo State with capital at Betijoque
historical_names.name: Rafael Rangel

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Wanka (Huanca) indigenous settlement in the Mantaro Valley prior to Spanish reducción
historical_names.name: Chupaka

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish Toledan reducción and parish of San Juan Bautista de Chupaca
historical_names.name: San Juan Bautista de Chupaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Peruvian republican district of Chupaca created by Ley of 2 January 1857
historical_names.name: Chupaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern coastal town and port established around the 1919 Packing House (municipality since 7 February 2002)
historical_names.name: Coveñas

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 18 July 1860 during the Colonización Antioqueña as Villa Rica de Segovia
historical_names.name: Villa Rica de Segovia

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Marsella in 1905 upon creation of Caldas Department to distinguish it from Segovia, Antioquia
historical_names.name: Marsella

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial foundation on the Paria Peninsula in 1713
historical_names.name: Río Caribe

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional founding year of the settlement and parish of Cáchira (municipality since 1911)
historical_names.name: Cáchira

historical_names.date_source_note: Shell oil camp and settlement of Casabe established in 1941 across the Magdalena River from Barrancabermeja
historical_names.name: Casabe

historical_names.date_source_note: Ordenanza 21 of 29 November 1978 elevating Yondó to a municipality of Antioquia
historical_names.name: Yondó

historical_names.date_source_note: Planned town built by Creole Petroleum Corporation for the Amuay Refinery (1949–1951)
historical_names.name: Judibana

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the town of Ayacucho by José Zoilo Miguens (Partido created 19 July 1865)
historical_names.name: Ayacucho

historical_names.date_source_note: Ley N° 15611 creating the District of Ignacio Escudero (capital San Jacinto)
historical_names.name: Ignacio Escudero

historical_names.date_source_note: Indigenous Caquetío and Jirajara settlement in the Yaracuy valley prior to colonial reducción
historical_names.name: Orachiche

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial pueblo de doctrina founded c. 1620 under Governor Francisco de la Hoz Berrío
historical_names.name: San Juan Bautista de Urachiche

historical_names.date_source_note: Venezuelan republican town and canton name
historical_names.name: Urachiche

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 20 January 1748 by José Fernando de Mier y Guerra in the Province of Santa Marta
historical_names.name: San Sebastián de Buenavista

historical_names.date_source_note: Distrito (later Municipio) Miranda in Mérida State, attested in the 1873 Venezuelan national census (capital Timotes)
historical_names.name: Miranda

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Ciudad de La Punta (San Luis Province) on 26 March 2003
historical_names.name: La Punta

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous Municipio Bolívar in Sucre State (capital Marigüitar) established under the 1989 Venezuelan municipal reform
historical_names.name: Bolívar

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1832 during the Colonización Antioqueña (erected as parish/district in 1832–1834)
historical_names.name: Pácora

historical_names.date_source_note: Indigenous Leco settlement and colonial mission in Larecaja Province, documented prior to Bolivian independence (municipality since 1991)
historical_names.name: Mapiri

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as Pedro Gual Municipality in Miranda State in 1992 (seat at Cúpira)
historical_names.name: Pedro Gual

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 25 December 1858 as San Antonio de Támesis during the Antioquian colonization
historical_names.name: San Antonio de Támesis

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as a municipality in Antioquia in 1864 under the official name Támesis
historical_names.name: Támesis

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Pijao/Carib settlement name (Natagaima) along the upper Magdalena River
historical_names.name: Natagaima

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reduction founded by Juan de Borja on 12 June 1608
historical_names.name: San Juan de Natagaima

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as a republican municipality in Tolima in 1863 under the official name Natagaima
historical_names.name: Natagaima

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Quechua/Aymara toponym (Asankaru / Hatun Asankaru) in the Azángaro basin, Puno
historical_names.name: Asankaru

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reduction and parish foundation c. 1586 in Puno
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de la Asunción de Azángaro

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated capital of Azángaro Province by decree of 21 June 1825; modern official name Azángaro
historical_names.name: Azángaro

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial frontier fort established on 18 November 1779 under Viceroy Vértiz
historical_names.name: Guardia del Monte

historical_names.date_source_note: Confirmed as head town of Monte Partido in Buenos Aires Province under the 1864 territorial law
historical_names.name: San Miguel del Monte

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested colonial parish in the Province of Cartagena (1779 census; modern official municipal name Santa Catalina)
historical_names.name: Santa Catalina

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 14 October 1776 as Hatoviejo in Cundinamarca
historical_names.name: Hatoviejo

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Villapinzón in 1904 in honour of General Próspero Pinzón
historical_names.name: Villapinzón

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as an autonomous commune of Chile by the Decree of 22 December 1891
historical_names.name: San Esteban

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Barranca District in Loreto by Law of 2 January 1857 (district seat later moved to San Lorenzo)
historical_names.name: Barranca

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as Distrito Roscio in Yuruari/Bolívar in 1881 (seat at Guasipati), now Municipio Roscio
historical_names.name: Roscio

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara/Quechua toponym (Pallqa) in the valley southeast of La Paz
historical_names.name: Pallqa

historical_names.date_source_note: Hispanicized colonial toponym documented from the late 16th-century Viceregal period in La Paz; continued as official Bolivian municipal name
historical_names.name: Palca

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as a municipality of Córdoba Department by Ordinance 005 of 17 April 1997 (previously a corregimiento of Lorica)
historical_names.name: Cotorra

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Chaná-Timbú settlement name (Corondá) along the Paraná branch
historical_names.name: Corondá

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish settlement of Coronda founded on 28 March 1664 by Melchor Martínez
historical_names.name: Coronda

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 7 September 1880 by provincial decree in Entre Ríos (as Colonia Federal, modern official city name Federal)
historical_names.name: Federal

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Cura Mori District in Piura Province by Law No. 15434 on 19 February 1965 (capital at Cucungará)
historical_names.name: Cura Mori

historical_names.date_source_note: Established around the San Justo railway station and agricultural colony in Uruguay Department, Entre Ríos, c. 1891
historical_names.name: San Justo

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as the municipality of Albán (seat San José de Albán) in Nariño in 1903 in honour of General Carlos Albán
historical_names.name: Albán

historical_names.date_source_note: Late-19th-century official town name in Trujillo State (previously Sabana Larga; seat of San Rafael de Carvajal Municipality)
historical_names.name: Carvajal

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Chaima/Cumanagoto indigenous toponym of the upper Manzanares valley
historical_names.name: Cumanacoa

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial foundation as San Baltazar de los Arias on 18 February 1700
historical_names.name: San Baltazar de los Arias

historical_names.date_source_note: Republican adoption of the indigenous-derived name Cumanacoa (modern official name)
historical_names.name: Cumanacoa

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Qulla and Inca capital of Collasuyu (1450–1530); modern Hispanicized town name is Hatuncolla
historical_names.name: Hatun Qulla

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara Lupaca settlement (Sipita) on Lake Titicaca
historical_names.name: Sipita

historical_names.date_source_note: Documented as a colonial Lupaca reduction in Garci Diez de San Miguel's Visita de Chucuito (1567); modern official name Zepita
historical_names.name: Zepita

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as La Coipa District in San Ignacio Province, Cajamarca, by Law No. 15560 on 12 May 1965
historical_names.name: La Coipa

historical_names.date_source_note: Town established in Tucumán around the Ingenio Bella Vista sugar mill founded in 1882
historical_names.name: Bella Vista

historical_names.date_source_note: River crossing and settlement on the Paraná bluff known as Punta Gorda prior to the 1836 town foundation
historical_names.name: Punta Gorda

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded as Villa del Diamante (Diamante) on 27 February 1836 by decree of Governor Pascual Echagüe
historical_names.name: Diamante

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 14 May 1951 during the colonization of Caquetá; elevated to municipality in 1967
historical_names.name: El Doncello

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally listed as a civil parish of Azogues Canton under Ecuador's Ley de División Territorial of 29 May 1861, having developed earlier as a rural annex and ecclesiastical parish (also titled San José de Biblián) on historic Cañari territory; later elevated to Biblián Canton on 1 August 1944.
historical_names.name: Biblián

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as a rural agricultural locality in Tucumán in the Second Argentine National Census (10 May 1895); later organized as a rural commune in Yerba Buena Department under the same name.
historical_names.name: Cevil Redondo

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded around 1905 near the Upín salt mines in Meta as the settlement of La Concepción (also known as Salinas de Upín).
historical_names.name: La Concepción

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to municipality and officially established as Restrepo by National Decree No. 1072 of 4 December 1915 in honour of former Colombian President Carlos Eugenio Restrepo (following its 1912 renaming from La Concepción).
historical_names.name: Restrepo

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement established in the early 20th century along the Curbaradó River in the lower Atrato basin on Emberá territory as a corregimiento of Riosucio; serves as the municipal seat (cabecera municipal).
historical_names.name: Curbaradó

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipality of Carmen del Darién created from Riosucio by Departmental Ordinance No. 018 of the Assembly of Chocó on 22 September 2000, with Curbaradó as its cabecera municipal.
historical_names.name: Carmen del Darién

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled and organized in the mid-19th century as the village and corregimiento of El Hatillo (also called San José del Hatillo) within Roldanillo on historic Gorrones territory.
historical_names.name: El Hatillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to a district of the Sovereign State of Cauca and renamed Bolívar in 1884 in honour of Simón Bolívar.
historical_names.name: Bolívar

historical_names.date_source_note: Mid-17th-century colonial settlement along the Canal del Dique on former Mocaná territory, originally known as Arenal.
historical_names.name: Arenal

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganized and dedicated under the patronage of Saint Stanislaus Kostka (full ecclesiastical title San Estanislao de Kostka) in November 1776 during the late-colonial town-founding campaign in the Province of Cartagena; modern official municipal name is San Estanislao.
historical_names.name: San Estanislao

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial foundation on 17 July 1758 in the Partido de Tierradentro (Province of Cartagena) on former Mocaná territory; ecclesiastically dedicated as San Pablo de Polonuevo and continuously known civilly as Polonuevo.
historical_names.name: Polonuevo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muisca (Chibcha) settlement in the Zipazgo of Bacatá, attested in early colonial chronicles as Gachanzipá / Gachansipa.
historical_names.name: Gachanzipá

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial foundation on 5 September 1612 as a pueblo de indios in the Province of Santafé (ecclesiastically titled San Bartolomé de Gachancipá), continuing under the modern municipal name Gachancipá.
historical_names.name: Gachancipá

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded around 1913 during the expansion of the Magdalena banana zone as a settlement and corregimiento of Aracataca; elevated to an independent municipality by Departmental Ordinance No. 006 of 25 June 1996 under the same name.
historical_names.name: El Retén

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 4 March 1941 along the Quebrada Pailitas as a colonization settlement and corregimiento of Tamalameque; elevated to a municipality of Cesar Department in 1968 under the same name.
historical_names.name: Pailitas

historical_names.date_source_note: Autonomous municipality of Miranda created in Trujillo State on 30 January 1988 by separation from the former Distrito Betijoque, with El Dividive as its municipal capital.
historical_names.name: Miranda

historical_names.name: Urdaneta

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 6 November 1829 in the Province of Ocaña and named Convención in commemoration of the 1828 Convention of Ocaña; continuously known as Convención.

historical_names.name: Tusi

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reducción and doctrina annex under the patronage of Saint Anne established during the Toledan reducciones in the Corregimiento of Tarma (attested in late-16th-century pastoral visits and colonial records as Santa Ana de Tusi); later elevated to an independent district by Law No. 12548 on 12 January 1956.
historical_names.name: Santa Ana de Tusi

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as a sugar-mill and agricultural settlement in Tucumán in the Second Argentine National Census (10 May 1895), grown around the 19th-century Ingenio El Manantial; later organized as a rural commune in Lules Department under the same name.
historical_names.name: El Manantial

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Timoto-Cuica indigenous settlement of the Tabayes in the Chama River valley.
historical_names.name: Mucutabay

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial pueblo de doctrina founded in 1619 during the visita of Oidor Alonso Vázquez de Cisneros in the Province of Mérida (ecclesiastically titled San Antonio de Tabay); modern seat of Santos Marquina Municipality.
historical_names.name: Tabay

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara/Colla settlement on the northern shore of Lake Titicaca.
historical_names.name: Wankani

historical_names.date_source_note: Hispanicized Spanish colonial reducción and doctrina established during the Toledan reducciones (ecclesiastically titled Santiago de Huancané) in the Lake Titicaca basin; confirmed as capital of Huancané Province on 19 September 1827.
historical_names.name: Huancané

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara settlement in the eastern valleys of the Sica Sica / La Paz region.
historical_names.name: Inkisawi

historical_names.date_source_note: Hispanicized Spanish colonial pueblo and doctrina in the Corregimiento of Sica Sica (ecclesiastically titled San Miguel de Inquisivi); confirmed as capital of Inquisivi Province on 2 November 1844.
historical_names.name: Inquisivi

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1808 as a late-colonial gold-mining settlement along the Anorí River in Antioquia (ecclesiastically titled San Juan de Anorí); elevated to parish in 1814 and municipality in 1821 under the name Anorí.
historical_names.name: Anorí

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as a populated corregimiento in Bolívar Department in the 1912 Colombian National Census (originating as a rural Sabanas settlement in the late 19th century); elevated to a municipality in 1931 and incorporated into Sucre Department in 1966.
historical_names.name: San Pedro
