historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Deán Valdivia District in Islay Province, Arequipa, by Peruvian Law No. 11870 of 23 October 1952, with La Curva designated as its capital.
historical_names.name: Deán Valdivia

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest dated attestation from the carved foundation stone of its colonial church (8 October 1782), later documented in Francisco de Viedma's 1793 report; created as a municipality by law of 6 October 1926.
historical_names.name: Pasorapa

historical_names.date_source_note: Ceded by Salta Province and designated capital of the Territorio Nacional de Los Andes by Argentine National Law No. 4059 of 26 September 1902 (ratified by Decree of 19 May 1904; incorporated into Salta Province on 21 September 1943).
historical_names.name: San Antonio de los Cobres

historical_names.date_source_note: Definitive colonial urban foundation on 29 June 1761 by Captain Joseph Nicolás Maldonado Sotomayor under Viceroy Manuel de Amat y Junyent as Villa de San Pedro de Sacaba (following an earlier 1560 tambo at nearby Kjuru Pampa).
historical_names.name: Villa de San Pedro de Sacaba

historical_names.date_source_note: Republican designation as capital of Chapare Province on 10 June 1854 under President Manuel Isidoro Belzu, omitting the colonial Villa de San Pedro prefix.
historical_names.name: Sacaba

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 10 May 1882 with the establishment of the Ingenio Azucarero Las Palmas del Chaco Austral by Richard and Charles Hardy in Bermejo Department, Chaco.
historical_names.name: Las Palmas

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and seat of the Corregimiento de Yauyos established c. 1571-1573 under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's ordinances and documented by Corregidor Diego Dávila Briceño (1586).
historical_names.name: Santo Domingo de Atun Yauyo

historical_names.date_source_note: Republican creation of Yauyos Province by José de San Martín's decree of 4 August 1821, simplifying the capital name to Yauyos.
historical_names.name: Yauyos

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 19 March 1911 (Feast of Saint Joseph) by landowners Jesús Vaca Narvaja and Juan Cornejo as Pueblo San José.
historical_names.name: Pueblo San José

historical_names.date_source_note: Adopted the name Balnearia from its Ferrocarril Central Norte Argentino station (opened with the first train on 1 February 1913), named after nearby Laguna Mar Chiquita.
historical_names.name: Balnearia

historical_names.date_source_note: Initial foundation by Diego García de Paredes on 9 October 1557 in Escuque (relocated multiple times in the 1550s-1560s as Mirabel, Trujillo del Collado, Trujillo de Salamanca, and Trujillo de Medellín).
historical_names.name: Nueva Trujillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Permanent colonial establishment on 27 October 1570 in the Valle de los Mukas by Francisco de Labastida under the name Trujillo de Nuestra Señora de la Paz.
historical_names.name: Trujillo de Nuestra Señora de la Paz

historical_names.date_source_note: Independence-era republican simplification when Trujillo adhered to the Venezuelan independence movement on 9 October 1810 (later documented in the 1873 national census).
historical_names.name: Trujillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca provincial wamani capital in Collasuyu (Belén Department, Catamarca), occupied c. 1471-1536 CE, bearing its traditional Quechua/Kakán site toponym.
historical_names.name: Shincal de Quimivil

historical_names.date_source_note: Early Tolita phase of the pre-Columbian Tumaco-La Tolita culture in Esmeraldas (c. 600 BCE to 700 CE). The original indigenous name is unattested, so the established archaeological site toponym (derived from its earthen mounds or tolas) is used.
historical_names.name: La Tolita

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest documented indigenous toponym for the lower Aconcagua Valley settlement (archaeologically occupied from c. 400 CE through the Bato, Llolleo, and Aconcagua periods, and later an Inca wamani center).
historical_names.name: Quillota

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial villa founded on 11 November 1717 by interim Governor José de Santiago Concha y Salvatierra as Villa de San Martín de la Concha.
historical_names.name: Villa de San Martín de la Concha

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to city rank on 6 August 1822 by Supreme Director Bernardo O'Higgins under the title Ciudad de San Martín de Quillota.
historical_names.name: San Martín de Quillota

historical_names.date_source_note: Simplified republican administrative name attested when the Department of Quillota was incorporated into the newly created Valparaíso Province on 27 October 1842 (and in the 1875 census).
historical_names.name: Quillota

historical_names.date_source_note: Middle Horizon Wari ceremonial and ceramic-production center in Ayacucho (c. 500-1100 CE), bearing a traditional Quechua toponym (Qunchupata).
historical_names.name: Conchopata

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Columbian settlement in Durán, Guayas, reaching its demographic peak during the Integration Period (Milagro-Quevedo culture, c. 600-1400 CE). Its original indigenous name is unattested, so the modern archaeological site toponym is used.
historical_names.name: Peñón del Río

historical_names.date_source_note: Late Intermediate Period Lupaqa fortified hilltop settlement (pukara) above Juli, Puno (c. 1100-1430 CE, preceding Inca conquest and the colonial Toledan reducción at lakeshore Juli).
historical_names.name: Pucará de Juli

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded c. 1915-1918 by General Belisario Téllez on lands of Ezequiel Florián in Santander as Puerto Florián.
historical_names.name: Puerto Florián

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as an autonomous municipality under the simplified name Florián by Santander Decree No. 2355 of 14 August 1975 (having served as a departmental police inspection since 1944).
historical_names.name: Florián

historical_names.date_source_note: Mapudungun toponym in the ancestral Llaimamapu territory; urban settlement founded c. 1941 and formally established as a commune by DFL No. 1-2.868 (published 15 October 1980).
historical_names.name: Melipeuco

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 13 February 1844 as a parochial district segregated from Zapatoca under the patronage of San Bernardo by presbyter Pedro José Guarín Durán and local settlers.
historical_names.name: San Bernardo de Betulia

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as a parish and municipality on 6 July 1895 under its simplified modern name Betulia.
historical_names.name: Betulia

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of San Gabán District (Carabaya Province, Puno) by Ley N° 5214 on 15 October 1925, designating the pre-existing settlement of Lanlacuni Bajo as district capital.
historical_names.name: San Gabán

historical_names.date_source_note: Discovery of copper deposits and establishment of the Mineral de La Higuera mining settlement in 1844 (later constituted as a commune on 22 December 1891).
historical_names.name: La Higuera

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Columbian archaeological settlement site on the La Cabrera peninsula (Lake Valencia), occupied c. 200-1500 CE across the La Cabrera and Valencia ceramic phases (excavated by Alfred Kidder II in 1934; indigenous settlement name unattested).
historical_names.name: Los Tamarindos

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish foundation by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada on 8 March 1537 at the pre-Hispanic indigenous settlement of Chipatá (following the expedition's first Andean mass on 2 February 1537).
historical_names.name: Chipatá

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonization and founding of Cumbitara on 24 February 1897 (made a corregimiento of Los Andes in 1913 and erected as a municipality on 21 November 1968).
historical_names.name: Cumbitara

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial Toledan reducción (c. 1572-1575) established in the Pacajes/Machaca territory during Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's general resettlement; later made capital of José Manuel Pando Province on 29 May 1986.
historical_names.name: Santiago de Machaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the commune of Alto Biobío (separated from Santa Bárbara, with Villa Ralco as municipal seat) by Ley N° 19.959, promulgated 16 July 2004 and published 21 July 2004.
historical_names.name: Alto Biobío

historical_names.date_source_note: Original founding of the settlement of Venecia on 5 September 1924 within the jurisdiction of Pandi.
historical_names.name: Venecia

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as an autonomous municipality by Decree No. 727 / National Decree No. 2213 (23 October 1951) and named Ospina Pérez after President Mariano Ospina Pérez.
historical_names.name: Ospina Pérez

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Venecia by Cundinamarca Departmental Assembly Ordenanza No. 17 of 29 November 1974.
historical_names.name: Venecia

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal recognition as a pueblo under Simón Bolívar's 1825 administrative reorganization (near the 1542 Battle of Chupas site; later created as a district of Huamanga Province by law of 2 January 1857).
historical_names.name: Chiara

historical_names.date_source_note: Grant of the colonial encomienda of Cachi in 1673 following the Calchaquí Wars and earlier Diaguita/Inca occupation; later consolidated as the Hacienda de Cachi (18th century) and expanded after 1946 expropriation.
historical_names.name: Cachi

historical_names.date_source_note: Official foundation of the town of Chile Chico on 21 May 1929, following spontaneous Chilean pioneer settlement on the southern shore of Lago Buenos Aires from 1905 and the 1918 land conflict.
historical_names.name: Chile Chico

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca cacicazgo of Chitagoto contacted in 1537; colonial indigenous settlement annexed to Sativanorte in 1683, site of the original town.
historical_names.name: Chitagoto

historical_names.date_source_note: Parish and district erected on 1 March 1834 under the name La Paz; relocated to Huerta Grande on 20 July 1935 after the 23 November 1933 landslide.
historical_names.name: La Paz

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Paz de Río by Boyacá Departmental Assembly Ordenanza No. 6 of 31 March 1936, commemorating the 1934 Rio de Janeiro peace treaty.
historical_names.name: Paz de Río

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca cacicazgo (uzaque) of Suba on the Bogotá savanna (attested archaeologically in the Muisca period and documented at Spanish contact in 1537; colonial pueblo de indios later established in 1550).
historical_names.name: Suba

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial indigenous community of Ocros granted a Corona de España territorial title on 30 December 1660; later created as a district on 15 July 1936 by Ley N° 8501.
historical_names.name: Ocros

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1790 by Franciscan missionary Manuel Álvarez de Villanueva on the Huayabamba River; later recognized as a district in 1853/1866/1868.
historical_names.name: Pachiza

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Maranura District (La Convención Province, Cusco) by Ley N° 13620 on 15 March 1961, designating the town of Maranura (previously a rural hacienda area) as district capital.
historical_names.name: Maranura

historical_names.date_source_note: Metallurgical smelter settlement established c. 1906 by the Cerro de Pasco Copper Corporation.
historical_names.name: Smelter

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to Villa and renamed Tinyahuarco by Ley N° 1491 on 4 December 1911 (later created as a district by Ley N° 2443 on 12 September 1917).
historical_names.name: Tinyahuarco

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca royal estate and hilltop citadel (Pisaq) constructed c. 1440-1450 under Sapa Inca Pachacuti; the valley town was later established as a Toledan colonial reducción in the 1570s.
historical_names.name: Písac

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement consolidated c. 1853 as the hamlet (caserío) of Toldas within San Andrés de Cuerquia (traditional regional founding also cited as 19 January 1757; elevated to corregimiento in 1891).
historical_names.name: Toldas

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as a separate municipality named Córdoba by Antioquia Ordenanza No. 33 on 29 April 1912.
historical_names.name: Córdoba

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Toledo by Antioquia Ordenanza No. 22 on 29 May 1915 upon popular petition.
historical_names.name: Toledo

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as San Pedro de Guacaybamba in Viceroy Martín Enríquez de Almansa's 1583 relation and as a doctrina head during Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo's 1586/1593 visits (also documented in 1792 colonial land composition records).
historical_names.name: San Pedro de Huacaybamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Huacaybamba District on 2 January 1857 (later elevated to capital of Huacaybamba Province by Ley N° 24340 on 7 November 1985).
historical_names.name: Huacaybamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the settlement as Planadas by decree of the Sovereign State of Santander on 30 September 1877 (municipal district 3 September 1887).
historical_names.name: Planadas

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Concordia by Santander Departmental Assembly Ordenanza No. 39 of 1892.
historical_names.name: Concordia

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Ragonvalia by Norte de Santander Departmental Assembly Ordenanza No. 28 on 14 April 1930, honoring General Ramón González Valencia.
historical_names.name: Ragonvalia

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest official colonial attestation on 8 May 1663 in Expediente No. 598 as the estancia and settlement of San Antonio de Perico / Perico de San Antonio.
historical_names.name: Perico de San Antonio

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as administrative seat of San Antonio Department by Jujuy Provincial Law No. 537 on 26 November 1899.
historical_names.name: San Antonio

historical_names.date_source_note: Inauguration of Zavalla railway station on the Ferrocarril Oeste Santafesino on 4 November 1883 (following 1882 settlement; town officially laid out on 28 August 1887 and Comisión de Fomento created in July 1898).
historical_names.name: Zavalla

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest colonial attestation in Viceroy Martín Enríquez de Almansa's 1583 relation (as San Juan de Cacha/Racha) and Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo's 1593 visit (San Juan de Racha).
historical_names.name: San Juan de Racha

historical_names.date_source_note: Documented in 1596 communal/encomienda titles as San Juan de Chavín (subsequently known as San Juan de Chavinillo / Chavinillo).
historical_names.name: San Juan de Chavín

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Chavinillo District by Ley N° 203 on 14 September 1906 (later capital of Yarowilca Province on 9 June 1995).
historical_names.name: Chavinillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional colonial gold-mining and parish settlement (also historically referred to as Santa Rosa de Aucapata / Maukallajta) integrated into Muñecas Province upon its creation on 18 October 1826 (elevated to Third Municipal Section by Ley N° 1427 on 11 February 1993).
historical_names.name: Aucapata

historical_names.date_source_note: Approximate Inca establishment of the administrative centre (llacta) of Caxas in Guayacundo territory under Túpac Inca Yupanqui (c. 1475), attested as Caxas in 1532 Spanish conquest chronicles.
historical_names.name: Caxas

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Inca Omaguaca (Tilcara) hilltop settlement in the Quebrada de Humahuaca dated archaeologically to c. 1100–1200 CE.
historical_names.name: Tilcara

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca conquest and reorganisation as a fortified administrative centre (pukara/llacta) in Collasuyu under Túpac Inca Yupanqui (c. 1475–1480).
historical_names.name: Pucará de Tilcara

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Fundo Iberia in 1903 by Spanish rubber entrepreneurs Baldomero and Máximo Rodríguez after taking over the earlier Fundo Adriazola rubber camp along the Tahuamanu River.
historical_names.name: Fundo Iberia

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to Iberia District in Tahuamanu Province by Law No. 13656 on 7 June 1961.
historical_names.name: Iberia

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial pueblo de indios founded between 13 and 17 February 1592 by oidor Bernardino de Albornoz, continuing the pre-Hispanic Muisca settlement of the cacique Tibacuy.
historical_names.name: Tibacuy

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Zonda Department separating from Rivadavia on 7 March 1935 (municipal boundaries fixed 4 September 1942); its seat Villa Basilio Nievas was designated cabecera in December 1840 in the Zonda valley.
historical_names.name: Zonda

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested in 1689 ecclesiastical visita records (written 'Guaca') as a viceparish/anexo of the Curato de Caracoto; later constituted as Huata District by Regional Law No. 467 promulgated on 22 August 1921.
historical_names.name: Huata

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as a district of Chota Province by the Provisional Law of Municipalities on 2 January 1857 under President Ramón Castilla (previously within the colonial Corregimiento de los Huambos).
historical_names.name: Cochabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Frontier military outpost established in 1850 on the shores of Laguna El Chañar prior to the town's formal founding.
historical_names.name: Fortín El Chañar

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the town and agricultural colony of Teodelina on 30 July 1875 by Diego de Alvear and José Roberti.
historical_names.name: Teodelina

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Quijos Canton under the Gran Colombia Territorial Division Law of 25 June 1824 (restored definitively on 17 January 1955), continuing the 16th-century Quijos province and anchored by its cabecera Baeza (founded 14 May 1559).
historical_names.name: Quijos

historical_names.date_source_note: Founding decree of 21 September 1889 establishing the locality as Estación Renca (also known as Renca Nuevo), developed around the railway station from 1904.
historical_names.name: Estación Renca

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Tilisarao in 1925 (exact month/day unattested in public decree summaries) to avoid postal confusion with the nearby town of Renca.
historical_names.name: Tilisarao

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested c. 1797 as an Augustinian ecclesiastical anexo of the semiparroquia of Llaray.
historical_names.name: Cachicadán

historical_names.date_source_note: Recorded in 1834 municipal and documentary registers as the paraje of La Banda prior to thermal-bath settlement growth from 1835.
historical_names.name: La Banda

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to Cachicadán District in Santiago de Chuco Province by law of 3 November 1900.
historical_names.name: Cachicadán

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Santa Rosa created by Supreme Decree of 2 May 1854 in Chucuito Province (transferred to El Collao Province on 12 December 1991); its district seat was moved to Mazo Cruz (Mazocruz) by Decree Law No. 9783 on 22 January 1943.
historical_names.name: Santa Rosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Gold-mining settlement documented in the 1750s (c. 1759) as Real de Minas de Nuestra Señora de la Concepción prior to chapel construction in 1769 and parish erection on 6 November 1770.
historical_names.name: Real de Minas de Nuestra Señora de la Concepción

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional official founding and consolidation of the town and parish of Concepción on 8 September 1771 (following the parish decree of 6 November 1770).
historical_names.name: Concepción

historical_names.date_source_note: Documented as the curato/doctrina of Paucarbamba in Huanta Province by Cosmógrafo Mayor Cosme Bueno (c. 1760–1764); created as a district of Tayacaja Province by Simón Bolívar's decree of 21 June 1825 and transferred to Churcampa Province in 1985.
historical_names.name: Paucarbamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Guane seat of the Cacique Guanentá on the plateau known in Chibcha/Guane toponymy as Mesa de Xerira (c. 1000–1540), attested in 16th-century Spanish chronicles.
historical_names.name: Mesa de Xerira

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial settlement and parish of Los Santos founded on 1 January 1750 by Bartolomé Mantilla and Vicente Rueda, named after Quebrada del Santo (modern plateau known as Mesa de los Santos).
historical_names.name: Los Santos

historical_names.date_source_note: Initial muleteer waystation and hamlet established c. 1872 along the Puerto Berrío–Medellín route.
historical_names.name: San Felipe de las Barajas

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Sardinas de la Plata during the local gold-mining boom (traditional town founding commemorated on 8 June 1876).
historical_names.name: Sardinas de la Plata

historical_names.date_source_note: Adopted the name Caracolí with the arrival of the Antioquia Railway station c. 1897; elevated to municipality on 30 November 1963.
historical_names.name: Caracolí

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 30 June 1911 by José Lutgardis Riveros Gigena and Ramona Gigena de Morcillo as Alcira (Estación Gigena); also commonly referred to municipally as Alcira Gigena.
historical_names.name: Alcira

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as Hacienda de Lagunas in Antonio Raimondi's geographic itineraries of northern Peru (1868); elevated to Lagunas District in Ayabaca Province by Law No. 10399 on 23 February 1946.
historical_names.name: Lagunas

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested as Hacienda Sacabamba during the 1781 indigenous uprising led by Martín Uchu in the Tarata/Cliza jurisdiction; created as the fourth municipal section of Esteban Arze Province by Law No. 1195 on 1 November 1990.
historical_names.name: Sacabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Year of initial permanent settlement established by municipal historical investigation (1905); cadastral town survey completed on 6 August 1951.
historical_names.name: El Espinillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Kallawaya settlement in Larecaja attested in early 17th-century colonial administrative and cacique testimonies (1618); constituted as a municipality in Bautista Saavedra Province by Law No. 546 on 13 May 1983.
historical_names.name: Curva

historical_names.date_source_note: Toledo-era indigenous reducción and repartimiento of Cabanilla (written 'Cauanilla' in the 1572–1575 Visita General of Viceroy Francisco de Toledo); created as a district of Lampa Province by Bolívar's decree of 21 June 1825.
historical_names.name: Cabanilla

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 19 May 1903 around the Estación Las Liebres railway station, named after the nearby estancia El Corral de Las Liebres.
historical_names.name: Las Liebres

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Laborde on 13 December 1919 after landowner Juan María Laborde.
historical_names.name: Laborde

historical_names.date_source_note: Rural parish established on 1 January 1941 (executive accord of 9 January 1941) in Saraguro Canton; its cabecera was renamed 28 de Mayo after the 28 May 1944 Revolution.
historical_names.name: San José de Yacuambi

historical_names.date_source_note: Canton of Yacuambi created by Legislative Decree of 8 January 1953 (published in Registro Oficial No. 360 on 10 November 1953) in Zamora Chinchipe Province, with cabecera 28 de Mayo.
historical_names.name: Yacuambi

historical_names.date_source_note: District created by Law No. 15136 on 8 September 1964 in Alto Amazonas Province, with capital at the riverside settlement of Shucushuyacu.
historical_names.name: Teniente César López Rojas

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonisation settlement of Pumahuasi established along the Huánuco–Pucallpa road (circa 1937–1938) prior to district creation.
historical_names.name: Pumahuasi

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Daniel Alomía Robles created by Law No. 11843 on 27 May 1952, with Pumahuasi designated as capital.
historical_names.name: Daniel Alomía Robles

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Potoni created by Supreme Decree on 2 May 1854 under President José Rufino Echenique.
historical_names.name: Potoni

historical_names.date_source_note: Early colonial encomienda and indigenous settlement of La Cochuna granted by Francisco Pizarro to Lucas Martínez Begazo on 22 January 1540.
historical_names.name: La Cochuna

historical_names.date_source_note: Segregated from the doctrina of Moquegua in 1619 by Bishop Pedro Perea y Grimaldo as the Doctrina of San Agustín de Torata.
historical_names.name: San Agustín de Torata

historical_names.date_source_note: Converted from colonial doctrina to the republican District of Torata under the Peruvian Constitution promulgated on 12 November 1823.
historical_names.name: Torata

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca settlement of the Chíos indigenous group at Pauso (modern Pueblo Viejo), documented prior to Spanish conquest (circa 1537).
historical_names.name: Pauso

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern town of Gama founded in 1870 by Juan Martín Romero; erected as a municipality by Ordinance No. 14 on 12 May 1903.
historical_names.name: Gama

historical_names.date_source_note: Created by Córdoba provincial decree in 1895 as Estación Quilino (surveyed 1897) around the Ferrocarril Central railway station near historic Villa Quilino (1796); commonly and administratively known as Quilino.
historical_names.name: Quilino

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca settlement of the Poasaque group; formally established as a colonial pueblo de doctrina on 9 September 1621 and elevated to parish on 26 January 1790.
historical_names.name: Chitaraque

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditionally founded on 18 April 1770; formally erected as an independent parish under the patronage of Nuestra Señora del Campo y San Vicente Ferrer on 18 April 1777.
historical_names.name: Ocamonte

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Llaylla created by Law No. 15481 on 26 March 1965 upon the establishment of Satipo Province.
historical_names.name: Llaylla

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Yunka/Inca settlement and sanctuary of Mama in the lower Rímac valley prior to Spanish conquest.
historical_names.name: Mama

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and doctrina of San Pedro de Mama established during Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's General Visitation (circa 1570–1573).
historical_names.name: San Pedro de Mama

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Ricardo Palma created and renamed by Law No. 9964 on 15 September 1944 in honour of Peruvian writer Ricardo Palma.
historical_names.name: Ricardo Palma

historical_names.date_source_note: Small rural settlement in Cerro Largo Department with no formal founding act; earliest official demographic attestation is the 1963 Uruguayan INE census (217 inhabitants).
historical_names.name: Toledo

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally founded as Villa Hernandarias by Entre Ríos Provincial Law No. 1875 promulgated on 28 May 1872 near the historic crossing of Paso Viejo / Arroyo Hernandarias.
historical_names.name: Villa Hernandarias

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled in the 1870s and established around 1881 by Salvador Lavalle; district of Vichayal created by Regional Law No. 316 on 28 August 1920 with San Felipe de Vichayal as capital.
historical_names.name: Vichayal

historical_names.date_source_note: Settlement of Managrú, the future municipal seat, established along the San Pablo River circa 1876.
historical_names.name: Managrú

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipality of El Cantón del San Pablo created from Istmina by Chocó Departmental Ordinance No. 004 on 23 May 1994, with Managrú as municipal seat.
historical_names.name: El Cantón del San Pablo

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded on 12 June 1937 by Domingo Minetti y Hijos Ltda.; commune established on 28 June 1940 and declared a city on 23 May 2024.
historical_names.name: Villa Minetti

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded on 29 October 1904 with the inauguration of Estación Tintina on the railway branch.
historical_names.name: Tintina

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and doctrina of Pusi (under the patronage of San Juan Bautista) established during Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's General Visitation in the 1570s; transferred from Azángaro to Huancané Province by Supreme Decree on 2 May 1854.
historical_names.name: Pusi

historical_names.date_source_note: Agricultural settlement of Sinchao Grande (Sinchao) established circa 1879 on lands adjudicated by the Catacaos peasant community.
historical_names.name: Sinchao Grande

historical_names.date_source_note: District of El Tallán created by Law No. 15434 on 19 February 1965, with Sinchao designated as its capital.
historical_names.name: El Tallán

historical_names.date_source_note: Military outpost Fortín Añelo established at Paso del Añelo on the Neuquén River during the Conquest of the Desert campaign (1879–1883).
historical_names.name: Fortín Añelo

historical_names.date_source_note: Town of Añelo officially founded by National Executive Decree on 20 October 1915 as seat of Añelo Department.
historical_names.name: Añelo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Sutagao indigenous settlement documented prior to Spanish conquest (circa 1537).
historical_names.name: Pandi

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial pueblo de indios formally designated San Francisco de Pandi upon the grant of resguardo lands circa 1754.
historical_names.name: San Francisco de Pandi

historical_names.date_source_note: Parish founded on 15 July 1793 by Oidor Juan Agustín de Chávez y García at Quinsuopaca under the name Santísima Trinidad de Pandi.
historical_names.name: Santísima Trinidad de Pandi

historical_names.date_source_note: Incorporated into the republican administrative framework under the Gran Colombia Territorial Division Law of 25 June 1824 (Canton of Fusagasugá, Cundinamarca) as Pandi.
historical_names.name: Pandi

historical_names.date_source_note: District of San Rafael created by Law No. 10164 on 5 January 1945 under President Manuel Prado Ugarteche, following earlier settlement by pioneer Rafael Isuiza.
historical_names.name: San Rafael

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded on 12 October 1920 with the arrival of the first settler family (Enrique Graef) on lands acquired by Carlos Culmey in 1919.
historical_names.name: Capioví

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1830 in the area previously known as El Morrón as a dependency of Cocorná; elevated to municipality on 16 February 1986.
historical_names.name: San Francisco

historical_names.date_source_note: Civil parish of Santa Rosalía erected on 5 April 1795 (ecclesiastical decree 15 April 1795) by segregation from San Pablo parish, following the 1696 votive hermitage in Sabana del Viento.
historical_names.name: Santa Rosalía

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca-era tambo and valley settlement of Jaquijahuana (Xaquixaguana) in the Cuzco heartland; dataset earliest_year is 1450.
historical_names.name: Jaquijahuana

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción and doctrina of Anta established in the Pampa de Anta during Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's General Visitation (1571–1572).
historical_names.name: Anta

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca frontier stronghold (cercado del Zipa) documented prior to the 1538 Spanish arrival; dataset earliest_year is 1000. Refounded as a colonial pueblo de indios at Teuta by Oidor Diego Gómez de Mena on 3 July 1600 under the same name.
historical_names.name: Facatativá

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to viceparish (viceparroquia) of Caracas Cathedral on 5 August 1676; temple construction begun in 1654 by the Cofradía de Nuestra Señora de Altagracia.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de Altagracia

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as an independent ecclesiastical parish of Caracas by Bishop Manuel Machado y Luna and Real Cédula of 25 August 1750 (modern Parroquia Altagracia; La Pastora split off on 16 October 1889).
historical_names.name: Parroquia Altagracia

historical_names.date_source_note: Initial settlement name around the Santa Fe–Reconquista railway station opened on 1 September 1889 on lands of Ignacio Crespo.
historical_names.name: San Rómulo

historical_names.date_source_note: Official town layout surveyed and approved in 1897 under the name Gobernador Crespo, honouring former Santa Fe governor Domingo Crespo.
historical_names.name: Gobernador Crespo

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest dataset archaeological horizon (c. 500 CE) for the pre-Hispanic Comechingón/Sanavirón settlement along the Suquía River, documented as Quisquisacate in the 6 July 1573 founding charter of Córdoba; replaces synthetic ethnic label 'Suquía Comechingón'.
historical_names.name: Quisquisacate

historical_names.date_source_note: Late Formative pre-Columbian urban ceremonial centre in Lampa, Puno (c. 400 BCE–400 CE), attested under the Puquina/Quechua toponym Pukara (modern Pucará).
historical_names.name: Pukara

historical_names.date_source_note: Institutional founding with the creation of the Comisión de Fomento on 9 December 1938 (elevated to municipality in 1946; river port area also called Puerto Panambí).
historical_names.name: Panambí

historical_names.date_source_note: Agricultural colony founded in October 1870 by Mauricio Franck, Ricardo Foster, and the Province of Santa Fe.
historical_names.name: Colonia Franck

historical_names.date_source_note: Comuna de Franck formally established on 4 January 1884, consolidating the town name Franck.
historical_names.name: Franck

historical_names.date_source_note: Agricultural colony founded in 1868 by Camilo Aldao and José María Cullen (local municipality established on 2 September 1874 as Jesús María).
historical_names.name: Colonia Jesús María

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Timbúes in 1974 after the local railway station (opened 1892) to avoid postal confusion with Jesús María, Córdoba.
historical_names.name: Timbúes

historical_names.date_source_note: Town of Yuto founded on 3 August 1888 by Antonio Abad Hinestroza and Rudecindo Palacios within Quibdó municipality.
historical_names.name: Yuto

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipality of Atrato created on 9 May 1997 by Chocó Ordinance 010, separating from Quibdó with Yuto as municipal seat.
historical_names.name: Atrato

historical_names.date_source_note: Jesuit-Guaraní reduction founded on 8 December 1619 by San Roque González de Santa Cruz.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de la Limpia Concepción del Ibitiracuá

historical_names.date_source_note: Refounded and surveyed on 27 September 1877 by the Corrientes government over the ruins of the former Jesuit mission as Concepción de la Sierra.
historical_names.name: Concepción de la Sierra

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as an official village (aldea) by ordinance of the Provincial Assembly of Tunja on 22 October 1856 (elevated to district/municipality on 28 December 1866).
historical_names.name: Arcabuco

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Conchán created on 4 November 1889 (ratified by Law of 13 October 1891); previously a colonial estate (Hacienda de Conchán) in Chota.
historical_names.name: Conchán

historical_names.date_source_note: Institutional founding of Ullum Department on 23 December 1913 (municipal seat at Villa Ibáñez; name derived from the pre-Hispanic Huarpe toponym Ullum/Ullumpa).
historical_names.name: Ullum

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial doctrine and repartimiento of Omacha (Chilques y Masques) structured under Viceroy Toledo's 1570s reductions (attested in 1792 colonial tribute records; republican district created on 2 January 1857).
historical_names.name: Omacha

historical_names.date_source_note: District of San José de Quero created by Law No. 12373 on 28 June 1955, designating San José de Quero as district capital.
historical_names.name: San José de Quero

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as an independent municipality of Cainguás Department by Misiones Law XV No. 19 on 2 July 2020 (previously a settlement within Aristóbulo del Valle).
historical_names.name: Salto Encantado

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Calamarca created by Law No. 25261 on 19 June 1990 within the newly established Julcán Province.
historical_names.name: Calamarca

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 7 April 1768 by Bartolomé Cardozo at the site known as Las Mangas prior to relocation.
historical_names.name: Las Mangas

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated by 1778 (following 1771–1778 moves) to its present upland site under the name Alpujarra; erected as municipal district on 13 October 1887.
historical_names.name: Alpujarra

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional Aymara locality of Tumarapi, designated capital when Cantón Waldo Ballivián was created over its territory by Law No. 247 on 26 September 1963.
historical_names.name: Tumarapi

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as the Sixth Municipal Section (Municipio Waldo Ballivián) of Pacajes Province by Law No. 1087 on 21 February 1989, with Tumarapi as municipal seat.
historical_names.name: Waldo Ballivián

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Andarapa created by Law No. 9357 on 14 March 1941; previously a colonial indigenous community and doctrine settlement in the Andahuaylas valley.
historical_names.name: Andarapa

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated from canton to Second Municipal Section of Mizque Province by Law of 28 November 1941 (from Aymara Wila Wila; capital also designated Villa Eufronio Viscarra by Law of 3 December 1942).
historical_names.name: Vila Vila

historical_names.date_source_note: First attested as Pedernales in colonial cartography of 1732; formal settlement founded c. 1755 (first capital of Territorio Federal Delta, 1884–1887).
historical_names.name: Pedernales

historical_names.date_source_note: Resort town formally laid out in 1897 on lands of Hacienda de Pullally; bay first named Papudo in May 1536 by Alonso Quintero after cacique Carande ('el Papudo'), commune created 14 May 1927.
historical_names.name: Papudo

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Salpo created by Law of 24 December 1847 under President Ramón Castilla (transferred from Huamachuco to Otuzco Province in 1861; colonial mining and doctrina area).
historical_names.name: Salpo

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded on 10 October 1932 by Santiago del Estero Provincial Law No. 1176 along the railway line (earlier known informally during railway construction as Kilómetro 325 / Punta de Riel).
historical_names.name: Pampa de los Guanacos

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Oxamarca created by Law No. 4860 on 23 December 1923 (previously a pre-Hispanic cacicazgo and colonial estate San Agustín de Oxamarca).
historical_names.name: Oxamarca

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Huaso District and Julcán Province by Law No. 25261 on 19 June 1990; previously a rural caserío in Salpo District, Otuzco Province.
historical_names.name: Huaso

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested in the 1792 colonial viceroyalty census as a doctrina/parish in Partido de Cotabambas, Intendencia del Cusco, centred on the colonial church of San Matías de Mara.
historical_names.name: San Matías de Mara

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Mara District on 2 January 1857 under President Ramón Castilla.
historical_names.name: Mara

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal establishment and ratification of the indigenous reducción pueblo of Nimaima on 3 November 1621 by Archbishop Fernando Arias de Ugarte and Audiencia President Juan de Borja (earlier Panche community visited 1595.3.16; institutional town founding also cited as 1710; municipality erected 1882.12.13).
historical_names.name: Nimaima

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca provincial administrative-military centre in Chuquibamba District, Chachapoyas (Amazonas), constructed under Túpac Yupanqui c. 1475 during the Inca conquest of the Chachapoyas.
historical_names.name: Cochabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Diaguita-Calchaquí fortified settlement in the Calchaquí/Yocavil Valley, Salta, occupied from the Regional Developments period c. 900 CE and later seat of Calchaquí resistance until 1659–1660.
historical_names.name: Tolombón

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial founding on 4 August 1778 by Intendant Marqués Domingo de Mena Hermosa under the name Palca, Santo Domingo de Mena Hermosa (commonly Santo Domingo de Palca), following the 1767 Cuartel Loma fort.
historical_names.name: Santo Domingo de Palca

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Palca District on 2 January 1857 (ratified by Law No. 6250 on 22 October 1928).
historical_names.name: Palca

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Zapatero District in Lamas Province by Law No. 12130 on 15 October 1954 under President Manuel A. Odría.
historical_names.name: Zapatero

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded as a caserío on 19 December 1845 under the indigenous name Arro by settlers from Santa Fe de Antioquia.
historical_names.name: Arro

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to municipal district on 2 September 1865 and renamed Giraldo in honour of former Antioquia governor Rafael María Giraldo.
historical_names.name: Giraldo

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reducción established under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's Visita General c. 1571–1572; documented as San Sebastián de Llusco in Francisco de Acuña's 1586 Relación Geográfica de Chumbivilcas.
historical_names.name: San Sebastián de Llusco

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Llusco District in Chumbivilcas Province by law of 2 January 1857 under President Ramón Castilla.
historical_names.name: Llusco

historical_names.date_source_note: Law of 10 March 1882 creating the agricultural colony Colonia Cerrito on the former Estancia El Cerrito.
historical_names.name: Colonia Cerrito

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal urban founding on 28 April 1887 by Sixto Perini and Antonio Angelini under the official name Pueblo Gobernador Racedo.
historical_names.name: Pueblo Gobernador Racedo

historical_names.date_source_note: 1969 Entre Ríos provincial decree under interventor Ricardo Favre officially renaming Pueblo Gobernador Racedo to Cerrito (exact month/day not specified in public summaries).
historical_names.name: Cerrito

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Jacas Grande District in Huamalíes Province by Law No. 4730 on 29 October 1923 under President Augusto B. Leguía.
historical_names.name: Jacas Grande

historical_names.date_source_note: Parish of Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Pulí created by archiepiscopal decree on 12 July 1800 (confirmed by viceregal decree 31 July 1800) on an earlier Panche site known as Chaquitulo.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Rosario de Pulí

historical_names.date_source_note: Restoration of Pulí as an autonomous republican municipality in 1889 following the repeal of Ordinance 33 of 1888.
historical_names.name: Pulí

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-1533 Cañari-Inca settlement at the archaeological site of Yacuviña, recorded as the first historical site of the cantonal seat Paccha.
historical_names.name: Yacuviña

historical_names.date_source_note: Second historical relocation of the Cañari settlement to Haripoto (Pueblo Viejo) in 1560.
historical_names.name: Haripoto

historical_names.date_source_note: Third relocation ordered by Real Audiencia of Quito decree on 13 July 1709 to Zuy Zuo Zurimpalta, establishing the town of Paccha.
historical_names.name: Paccha

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Cantón Atahualpa (El Oro) by Legislative Decree No. 160 on 25 April 1984, with Paccha as cantonal seat.
historical_names.name: Atahualpa

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Quechua toponym Amancay (Amankay) attested for the Inca-Chanca frontier valley settlement near the Pachachaca River.
historical_names.name: Amancay

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial founding on 3 November 1574 by visitador Nicolás Ruiz de Estrada as Villa de Santiago de los Reyes de Amancay.
historical_names.name: Villa de Santiago de los Reyes de Amancay

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated as Abancay, capital of the newly created Department of Apurímac on 28 April 1873 (elevated to city on 3 November 1874).
historical_names.name: Abancay

historical_names.date_source_note: Formal establishment of the town of Boyuibe (Cordillera Province, Santa Cruz) in 1924 via donation of 20 hectares by landowner Atanasio Galarse; later became a canton on 27 September 1926 and municipality by Law No. 1265 on 30 September 1991.
historical_names.name: Boyuibe

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of Santa Clara (Santa Bárbara Department, Jujuy) on 5 December 1920 on the earlier rural paraje known as El Arenal.
historical_names.name: Santa Clara

historical_names.date_source_note: First official appearance of Estación Toledo (Ferrocarril Central Argentino) in railway timetables on 1 November 1889, adopted as founding reference date by municipal historical research.
historical_names.name: Toledo

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to the category of pueblo as Chullín (also San Juan de Chullín) by Law No. 1153 on 6 November 1909 within Sicsibamba District.
historical_names.name: Chullín

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of San Juan District in Sihuas Province by Law No. 14963 on 14 March 1964, with Chullín as district capital.
historical_names.name: San Juan

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern town in Almirante Brown Department, Chaco, founded by National Executive Decree on 7 December 1934 (surveyed 1932, Comisión de Fomento 1936), named in homage to the destroyed 1585–1632 colonial city whose ruins lie separately near Tres Isletas.
historical_names.name: Concepción del Bermejo

historical_names.date_source_note: Hispanic colonial pueblo de indios and doctrina founded on 16 July 1556 on the pre-Hispanic Muisca cacicazgo of Sáchica.
historical_names.name: Sáchica

historical_names.date_source_note: Declared an official pueblo on 1 June 1699 under the name San Bartolomé de Déleg, previously administered under the Doctrina de San Bartolomé de Cojitambo.
historical_names.name: San Bartolomé de Déleg

historical_names.date_source_note: Cantonization of Déleg on 27 February 1992 under President Rodrigo Borja, formalizing Déleg as cantonal seat.
historical_names.name: Déleg

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial settlement and chapel founded c. 1605 by encomendero Juan Buenaventura de la Carrera around devotion to the Virgen de la Natividad; later recognized as a district in the Independence era (1821–1825) and elevated to Villa on 9 November 1899.
historical_names.name: Huancaspata

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial Toledan reducción founded on 15 August 1572 under the name La Asunción de Matahuasi, consolidating earlier Huanca settlements (Hatunhuasi).
historical_names.name: La Asunción de Matahuasi

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of Matahuasi District by law of 23 October 1896 under President Nicolás de Piérola.
historical_names.name: Matahuasi

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Muisca settlement and cacicazgo under the Zipa of Bacatá, occupied from c. 1000 CE until Spanish conquest in 1538.
historical_names.name: Bosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial doctrina and pueblo de indios consolidated around the Church of San Bernardino de Bosa, built c. 1618 following the 1538 Spanish arrival.
historical_names.name: San Bernardino de Bosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Annexed to the Special District of Bogotá as Bosa on 17 December 1954 (modern Localidad 7).
historical_names.name: Bosa

historical_names.date_source_note: Town founded on 1 January 1902 around Cañada Verde railway station (opened 1 December 1901) on Estancia Cañada Verde.
historical_names.name: Cañada Verde

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Villa Huidobro by Córdoba provincial executive decree in 1907 in honour of General José Ruiz Huidobro (exact month/day not specified in public summaries).
historical_names.name: Villa Huidobro

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 12 February 1882 by Col. Ernesto Rodríguez as Victorica (honouring Minister of War Gen. Benjamín Victorica), the first town founded in La Pampa Territory.
historical_names.name: Victorica

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as El Milagro District in Utcubamba Province, Amazonas (Law No. 23843 of 30 May 1984), elevating the lower Utcubamba caserío to district capital.
historical_names.name: El Milagro

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest documented hamlet name when Soledad Argote donated lands in 1837 for the church and plaza (designated inspección de policía under this name in 1892).
historical_names.name: Las Llanadas

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Belén in 1929 (later made ecclesiastical parish in 1953 and municipality by Ordinance No. 53 of 20 January 1986).
historical_names.name: Belén

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial Hispanic settlement founded around 1683 by José Esteban and Lorenzo de Rojas on the Carcasí encomienda (following a c. 1600 doctrinero chapel at Victarigua).
historical_names.name: Carcasí

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as an ecclesiastical parish on 23 March 1772 under the patronage of San Juan de Sahagún de Carcasí.
historical_names.name: San Juan de Sahagún de Carcasí

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as a municipality of Santander Department by decree of 30 September 1887 under its modern short name.
historical_names.name: Carcasí

historical_names.date_source_note: Earliest Spanish cartographic attestation (1527 Carta Universal) naming the island Santa Catalina under Spanish claim (1510).
historical_names.name: Santa Catalina

historical_names.date_source_note: Settled on 22 March 1629 by English Puritans of the Providence Island Company (capital New Westminster), who named the island Providence / Old Providence.
historical_names.name: Old Providence

historical_names.date_source_note: Adhered to the Republic of Gran Colombia under the Constitution of Cúcuta on 23 June 1822 as Providencia (modern municipal seat at Santa Isabel).
historical_names.name: Providencia

historical_names.date_source_note: Hispanic foundation on 14 December 1556 by encomendero Antonio de Santana preserving the Muisca toponym Suta.
historical_names.name: Suta

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested by 1761 under the compound name Sutamarchán, combining Suta with the surname of 18th-century encomendero Capt. Pedro Merchán de Velasco (parish reforms 1776–1777).
historical_names.name: Sutamarchán

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded on 25 June 1858 as Villa Dolores at the earlier rural paraje of La Cruz during Gov. Justo Daract's administration.
historical_names.name: Villa Dolores

historical_names.date_source_note: Town formally adopted the name Concarán in 1934, following the 1904 naming of its railway station to avoid confusion with Villa Dolores, Córdoba.
historical_names.name: Concarán

historical_names.date_source_note: Indigenous ayllu reorganized under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo's colonial reducciones (1569–1573) in Anco, Huamanga; recognized as a district in the Independence era (c. 1825).
historical_names.name: Chungui

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially founded by national decree on 20 October 1915 designating the Mapudungun-named settlement as capital of Loncopué Department.
historical_names.name: Loncopué

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Alexander Von Humboldt District by Law No. 30310 on 16 March 2015; the roadside settlement (informally called Kilómetro 86) grew around the 1965 Alexander von Humboldt National Forest.
historical_names.name: Alexander Von Humboldt

historical_names.date_source_note: Official foundation of Villa de Saujil on 19 November 1869 (declared capital of Pomán Department on 29 September 1909).
historical_names.name: Saujil

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded in 1859 by four pioneer families (Matas Mestre, Mamaní, Llanos, and Gurrieri) in Ledesma Department.
historical_names.name: Caimancito

historical_names.date_source_note: San Nicolás District created on 5 February 1875 (from the colonial doctrina of San Nicolás de Bari attested in Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo's late-16th-century visits); its urban seat is officially named Mendoza.
historical_names.name: San Nicolás

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonization settlement founded on 14 October 1954 by R. G. LeTourneau, Inc. under a Peruvian government concession; later created as a district by Law No. 23994 on 19 November 1984.
historical_names.name: Tournavista

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Aymara oasis toponym attested at the onset of Spanish encomienda settlement c. 1540 following Diego de Almagro's 1535–1536 passage.
historical_names.name: Pica

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial parish established in 1620 by Bishop Pedro de Perea of Arequipa under the patronage of San Andrés de Pica.
historical_names.name: San Andrés de Pica

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as the Chilean commune of Pica on 22 December 1891 under the Autonomous Commune Law (later permanently re-established by Law No. 12.419 in January 1957).
historical_names.name: Pica

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded as Villa de San Fabián de Alico by supreme decree on 7 December 1865, promoted by Fabián de la Fuente Soto y Aguilar.
historical_names.name: San Fabián de Alico

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as the commune of San Fabián on 22 December 1891 under Chile's Autonomous Commune Law.
historical_names.name: San Fabián

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial land grant of Samo Alto issued to Capt. Martín de Elvira in 1579; constituted as the Commune of Samo Alto on 22 December 1891.
historical_names.name: Samo Alto

historical_names.date_source_note: Commune renamed and reconstituted as Río Hurtado by Decree Law No. 2.868 of 26 October 1979, with Samo Alto remaining its administrative seat.
historical_names.name: Río Hurtado

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Ocobamba District by the Transitional Municipalities Law of 2 January 1857 under President Ramón Castilla (its modern administrative seat is Kelcaybamba).
historical_names.name: Ocobamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Hispanic Puquina settlement name recorded in regional historical tradition prior to Spanish colonial reorganization.
historical_names.name: Huayna Upina

historical_names.date_source_note: Reorganized as a colonial reducción and repartimiento under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo c. 1572–1575 (attested in 1792 colonial padrones; formalized as a district on 2 January 1857).
historical_names.name: Ubinas

historical_names.date_source_note: Inca military and administrative complex built in the Lunahuaná valley under Túpac Yupanqui during the conquest of the Huarco lordship (c. 1470–1480; abandoned c. 1530).
historical_names.name: Inkawasi

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Conchamarca District by Law No. 9165 on 5 September 1940 (installed 24 November 1940), from a Huallaga valley settlement visited by Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo (1581–1606).
historical_names.name: Conchamarca

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 3 May 1928 by Swiss colonizer Eugenio Lagier under the local hybrid Spanish-Guaraní toponym Santo Pipó.
historical_names.name: Santo Pipó

historical_names.date_source_note: Created as Pajarillo District by Law No. 13765 on 15 December 1961, elevating the pre-existing Huallaga river caserío opposite Juanjuí.
historical_names.name: Pajarillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Established in 1875 around the Central Argentine Railway station originally named Carcarañá Oeste on lands belonging to the Correa family.
historical_names.name: Carcarañá Oeste

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial curato and settlement in Chachapoyas attested in late-18th-century notarial records (e.g., 1782; approx. year; district created 1870-12-26).
